bookInfo.author: Sima Guang

sentences.zh: 資治通鑑 第170卷卷第一百七十

translations.literal: Comprehensive Mirror in Aid of Governance, Volume 170, Roll One Hundred Seventy
translations.idiomatic: Comprehensive Mirror in Aid of Governance, Volume 170

sentences.zh: 【陳紀四】　起強圍大淵獻，盡重光單閼，凡五年。

translations.literal: [Chen Records 4] From Qiangwei Dayuanxian through Chongguang Dan'e; five years in all.
translations.idiomatic: [Chen Records 4] From Qiangwei Dayuanxian through Chongguang Dan'e—five years in all.

sentences.zh: 春，正月，癸酉朔，日有食之。

translations.literal: In spring, the first month, on the jiaoyou new moon, there was a solar eclipse.
translations.idiomatic: In spring, the first month, on the jiaoyou new moon, a solar eclipse occurred.

sentences.zh: 尚書左僕射袁樞卒。

translations.literal: Left Vice Minister of the Secretariat Yuan Shu died.
translations.idiomatic: Left Vice Minister of the Secretariat Yuan Shu died.

sentences.zh: 乙亥，大赦，改元。

translations.literal: On yihai, a general amnesty was proclaimed and the era name was changed.
translations.idiomatic: On yihai, Chen proclaimed a general amnesty and changed the era name.

sentences.zh: 辛卯，帝祀南郊。

translations.literal: On xinmao, the emperor sacrificed at the southern suburb.
translations.idiomatic: On xinmao, the emperor sacrificed at the southern suburb.

sentences.zh: 壬辰，齊上皇還鄴。

translations.literal: On renchen, the retired emperor of Qi returned to Ye.
translations.idiomatic: On renchen, the retired emperor of Northern Qi returned to Ye.

sentences.zh: 己亥，周主耕籍田。

translations.literal: On jihai, the Zhou ruler ploughed the sacred field.
translations.idiomatic: On jihai, the ruler of Northern Zhou ploughed the sacred field.

sentences.zh: 二月，壬寅朔，齊主加元服，大赦。

translations.literal: In the second month, on the renyin new moon, the ruler of Qi came of age and a general amnesty was proclaimed.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month, on the renyin new moon, the ruler of Northern Qi came of age, and a general amnesty was proclaimed.

sentences.zh: 初，高祖為梁州，用劉師知為中書舍人。

translations.literal: At the beginning, when Gaozu was at Liang Province, he employed Liu Shizhi as Secretariat Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: In the beginning, when Chen Baxian served as governor of Liang Province, he appointed Liu Shizhi as Secretariat Attendant.

sentences.zh: 師知涉學工文，練習儀體，歷世祖朝，雖位宦不遷，而委任甚重，與揚州刺史安成王頊、尚書僕射到仲舉同受遺詔輔政。

translations.literal: Shizhi was versed in scholarship and skilled in literary composition, practiced ceremonial protocol, and through Emperor Shizu's reign, though his official rank did not advance, his trust and appointment were very heavy; together with Chen Xu, Prince of Ancheng, governor of Yang Province, and Dao Zhongju, Vice Minister of the Secretariat, he received the late emperor's testamentary charge to assist in government.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Shizhi was learned and skilled with the pen, well trained in ritual forms; through the reign of Chen Qian his rank never rose, yet he was entrusted with grave responsibility—together with Chen Xu, Prince of Ancheng and governor of Yangzhou, and Vice Minister Dao Zhongju he had received the late emperor's order to share in governing.

sentences.zh: 師知、仲舉恆居禁中，參決眾事，頊與左右三百人入居尚書省。

translations.literal: Shizhi and Zhongju constantly resided within the forbidden quarters, participating in deciding the multitude of affairs; Xu, with three hundred men on his left and right, entered and dwelt in the Ministry of State Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Shizhi and Zhongju constantly remained inside the palace, deciding public affairs together, while Xu quartered some three hundred companions in the Ministry of State Affairs.

sentences.zh: 師知見頊地望權勢為朝野所屬，心忌之，與尚書左丞王暹等謀出頊於外。

translations.literal: Shizhi, seeing that Xu's territorial standing and authority were what court and countryside looked to, harbored jealousy in his heart; together with Wang Xuan, Left Assistant of the Secretariat, and others he plotted to send Xu outside the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Shizhi saw that Xu's position and power commanded the court and the realm, and resented it; with Wang Xuan, the left assistant of the Secretariat, and others he plotted to post Xu away from the capital.

sentences.zh: 眾猶豫，未敢先發。

translations.literal: The multitude still hesitated and did not dare act first.
translations.idiomatic: The conspirators still hesitated and dared not strike first.

sentences.zh: 東宮通事舍人殷不佞，素以名節自任，又受委東宮，乃馳詣相府，矯敕謂頊曰：「今四方無事，王可還東府經理州務。」

translations.literal: Yin Buxian of the Eastern Palace General Service, by nature charged himself with reputation and integrity, and having also received appointment from the Eastern Palace, then galloped to the chief minister's quarters and, counterfeiting an edict, told Xu: "Now that the four quarters are without incident, Your Highness may return to your eastern residence to manage the prefectural affairs."
translations.idiomatic: Yin Buxian of the Eastern Palace general service, who prided himself on integrity and had been entrusted by the heir's establishment, rode at once to the chief minister's residence and forged an edict telling Xu: "The realm is at peace; Your Highness should return to your eastern residence and manage your prefectural affairs."

sentences.zh: 頊將出，中記室毛喜馳入見頊曰：「陳有天下日淺，國禍繼臻，中外危懼。

translations.literal: As Xu was about to depart, Mao Xi of the Central Secretariat galloped in to see Xu and said: "Chen's possession of the realm under Heaven has been brief; national calamities have come one after another; within and without all are in peril.
translations.idiomatic: As Xu was preparing to leave, Mao Xi of the central secretariat rushed in and said: "The Chen house has held the realm for only a short time; disasters have struck in succession, and danger presses on every side.

sentences.zh: 太后深惟至計，令王入省共康庶績。

translations.literal: The empress dowager has deeply weighed the supreme plan and orders Your Highness to enter the Secretariat and together bring peace to the people's labors.
translations.idiomatic: The empress dowager has given this grave matter her deepest thought and bids Your Highness enter the Secretariat and share in governing the realm.

sentences.zh: 今日之言，必非太后之意。

translations.literal: Today's words surely are not the empress dowager's intent.
translations.idiomatic: What you have just heard cannot be the empress dowager's intent.

sentences.zh: 宗社之重，願王三思，須更聞奏，無使奸人得肆其謀。

translations.literal: The weight of the altars of state—may Your Highness think thrice; you must enquire again and report back, and not let traitors achieve their schemes.
translations.idiomatic: The fate of the dynasty hangs on your decision—think carefully, obtain further confirmation from the throne, and do not let villains have their way.

sentences.zh: 今出外即受制於人，譬如曹爽，願作富家翁，其可得邪！」

translations.literal: If you go out now you will fall under others' control—as with Cao Shuang, who wished only to be a wealthy household head, could he obtain it!"
translations.idiomatic: Once you leave the capital you will be at others' mercy—like Cao Shuang, who only wished to live out his days as a rich private citizen yet could not even do that!"

sentences.zh: 頊遣喜與領軍將軍吳明徹籌之，明徹曰：「嗣君諒暗，萬機多闕。

translations.literal: Xu sent Xi to consult with Wu Mingche, commander of the palace guard; Mingche said: "The succeeding ruler is in mourning; the myriad affairs of state are largely neglected.
translations.idiomatic: Xu sent Xi to confer with Wu Mingche of the palace guard. Mingche said: "The new emperor is still in mourning and state affairs are in disarray.

sentences.zh: 殿下親實周、邵，當輔安社稷，願留中勿疑。」

translations.literal: Your Highness in person are the Zhou and Shao of this age and ought to support and settle the altars of state; I hope you will remain within and not doubt it."
translations.idiomatic: You are the Zhou and Shao of our age and ought to steady the realm—stay in the capital and do not hesitate."

sentences.zh: 頊乃稱疾，召劉師知，留之與語，使毛喜先入言於太后。

translations.literal: Xu then feigned illness, summoned Liu Shizhi, detained him in conversation, and sent Mao Xi ahead to speak to the empress dowager.
translations.idiomatic: Xu then pretended illness, summoned Liu Shizhi, and kept him talking while Mao Xi went ahead to the empress dowager.

sentences.zh: 太后曰：「今伯宗幼弱，政事並委二郎。

translations.literal: The empress dowager said: "Now Bozong is young and weak; government affairs are all entrusted to the two gentlemen.
translations.idiomatic: The empress dowager said: "Bozong is still young; government has been left entirely to those two ministers.

sentences.zh: 此非我意。」

translations.literal: This is not my intent."
translations.idiomatic: This was never my wish."

sentences.zh: 喜又言於帝。

translations.literal: Xi again spoke to the emperor.
translations.idiomatic: Xi spoke next to the emperor.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「此自師知等所為，朕不知也。」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "This was done by Shizhi and the others on their own; I did not know of it."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said: "That was Shizhi and the rest acting on their own—I knew nothing of it."

sentences.zh: 喜出，以報頊。

translations.literal: Xi went out and reported to Xu.
translations.idiomatic: Xi came out and reported to Xu.

sentences.zh: 頊囚師知，自入見太后及帝，極陳師知之罪，仍自草敕請畫，以師知付廷尉。

translations.literal: Xu imprisoned Shizhi, entered himself to see the empress dowager and the emperor, set forth Shizhi's crimes to the utmost, and himself drafted an edict requesting the imperial brush, turning Shizhi over to the Minister of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: Xu imprisoned Shizhi, went in person before the empress dowager and the emperor, laid out his crimes at length, drafted an edict for imperial signature, and handed Shizhi over to the Minister of Justice.

sentences.zh: 其夜，於獄中賜死。

translations.literal: That same night, in prison, he was granted death.
translations.idiomatic: That night he was ordered to take his own life in prison.

sentences.zh: 以到仲舉為金紫光祿大夫。

translations.literal: Dao Zhongju was made Grand Master of the Golden Seal and Purple Girdle.
translations.idiomatic: Dao Zhongju was made Grand Master with the Golden Seal and Purple Girdle.

sentences.zh: 王暹、殷不佞並付治。

translations.literal: Wang Xuan and Yin Buxian were also handed over for trial.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Xuan and Yin Buxian were also handed over for punishment.

sentences.zh: 不佞，不豁之弟也，少有孝行，頊雅重之，故獨得不死，免官而已。

translations.literal: Buxian was the younger brother of Yin Buhuo; from youth he had a reputation for filial conduct, and Xu deeply esteemed him, so he alone was not put to death but only stripped of office.
translations.idiomatic: Buxian was the younger brother of Yin Buhuo; known since youth for filial piety, he was highly regarded by Xu and therefore spared execution, punished only by removal from office.

sentences.zh: 王暹伏誅。

translations.literal: Wang Xuan was executed.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Xuan was executed.

sentences.zh: 自是國政盡歸於頊。

translations.literal: From this time the government of the realm passed entirely to Xu.
translations.idiomatic: From that moment state power belonged entirely to Xu.

sentences.zh: 右衛將軍會稽韓子高鎮領軍府，在建康諸將中士馬最盛，與仲舉通謀。

translations.literal: Han Zigao of Kuaiji, right guard general, guarded the commander of the palace guard's headquarters; among the generals at Jiankang his men and horses were the strongest, and he was in communication with Zhongju's conspiracy.
translations.idiomatic: Han Zigao of Kuaiji, right guard general, held the palace guard headquarters; among the commanders at Jiankang his forces were the strongest, and he was in league with Zhongju.

sentences.zh: 事未發。

translations.literal: The affair had not yet erupted.
translations.idiomatic: The plot had not yet broken out.

sentences.zh: 毛喜請簡人馬配子高，並賜鐵、炭，使修器甲。

translations.literal: Mao Xi requested selecting men and horses to assign to Zigao, and also bestowing iron and charcoal for him to repair weapons and armor.
translations.idiomatic: Mao Xi proposed assigning him picked troops and granting iron and charcoal to repair arms and armor.

sentences.zh: 頊驚曰：「子高謀反，方欲收執，何為更如是邪？」

translations.literal: Xu startled and said: "Zigao is plotting rebellion and is about to be arrested—why act further in this way?"
translations.idiomatic: Xu was alarmed: "Zigao is plotting rebellion and we are about to arrest him—why strengthen him further?"

sentences.zh: 喜曰：「山陵始畢，邊寇尚多，而子高受委前朝，名為杖順。

translations.literal: Xi said: "The imperial tomb ritual has only just been completed; border enemies are still numerous; Zigao received commission from the previous dynasty and is known for upholding obedience.
translations.idiomatic: Xi said: "The imperial funeral has only just ended and enemies still threaten the borders; Zigao served the previous reign and has the name of a loyal commander.

sentences.zh: 若收之，恐不時受首，或能為人患。

translations.literal: If he is arrested, I fear he will not promptly submit his head, but may become a scourge to men.
translations.idiomatic: Seize him abruptly and he may not surrender promptly—he could become a serious threat.

sentences.zh: 宜推心安誘，使不自疑，伺間圖之，一壯士之力耳。」

translations.literal: One ought to extend trust and reassure him so that he does not suspect himself; wait for an opportunity and plot against him—it is the strength of a single bold man."
translations.idiomatic: Put him at ease until he lets his guard down, then strike—no more than one resolute man's work."

sentences.zh: 頊深然之。

translations.literal: Xu deeply approved this.
translations.idiomatic: Xu wholly agreed.

sentences.zh: 仲舉既廢歸私第，心不自安。

translations.literal: Zhongju, having been removed and returned to his private residence, was ill at ease in heart.
translations.idiomatic: Deposed and sent home, Zhongju grew uneasy.

sentences.zh: 子郁，尚世祖妹信義長公主，除南康內史，未之官。

translations.literal: His son Yu had married the Princess of Trust and Righteousness, the late emperor's younger sister, and had been appointed internal steward of Nankang but had not yet taken up the post.
translations.idiomatic: His son Yu had married the Princess of Trust and Righteousness, the late emperor's sister, and been named internal steward of Nankang but had not yet departed for his post.

sentences.zh: 子高亦自危，求出為衡、廣諸鎮；

translations.literal: Zigao also felt himself in danger and sought appointment to the garrison commands of Heng and Guang;
translations.idiomatic: Zigao, feeling endangered, sought a posting to the garrisons of Heng and Guang;

sentences.zh: 郁每乘小輿，蒙婦人衣，與子高謀。

translations.literal: Yu each time rode in a small carriage, veiled in woman's dress, and plotted with Zigao.
translations.idiomatic: Yu would ride in a small carriage disguised as a woman and meet Zigao in secret.

sentences.zh: 會前上虞令陸昉及子高軍主告其謀反。

translations.literal: Just then the former magistrate of Shangyu, Lu Fang, and Zigao's army supervisor reported their conspiracy to rebel.
translations.idiomatic: Then the former magistrate of Shangyu, Lu Fang, and an officer of Zigao's command denounced the plot.

sentences.zh: 頊在尚書省，因召文武在位議立皇太子。

translations.literal: Xu was at the Ministry of State Affairs; thereupon he summoned civil and military officials in post to deliberate establishing the crown prince.
translations.idiomatic: Xu was in the Ministry of State Affairs and summoned officials to discuss installing the crown prince.

sentences.zh: 平旦，仲舉、子高入省，皆執之，並郁送廷尉，下詔，於獄賜死，餘黨一無所問。

translations.literal: At dawn Zhongju and Zigao entered the Secretariat and were both seized; together with Yu they were sent to the Minister of Justice; an edict was issued, and in prison they were granted death; the remaining accomplices were not pursued at all.
translations.idiomatic: At dawn Zhongju and Zigao entered the ministry and were seized; with Yu they were sent to the Minister of Justice, where an edict condemned them to death in prison; none of their followers were pursued.

sentences.zh: 辛亥，南豫州刺史余孝頃坐謀反誅。

translations.literal: On xinhai, Yu Xiaogui, governor of southern Yuzhou, was executed for plotting rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: On xinhai, Yu Xiaogui, governor of Southern Yuzhou, was executed for treason.

sentences.zh: 癸丑，以東揚州刺史始興王伯茂為中衛大將軍、開府儀同三司。

translations.literal: On guichou, Chen Bamao, Prince of Shixing, was made commander of the central guard, grand general, and commissioner with the same ceremonial as the Three Excellencies.
translations.idiomatic: On guichou, Chen Bamao, Prince of Shixing, was made central guard commander and commissioner equal to the Three Excellencies.

sentences.zh: 伯茂，帝之母弟也，劉師知、韓子高之謀，伯茂皆預之；

translations.literal: Bamao was the emperor's younger uterine brother; in the plots of Liu Shizhi and Han Zigao Bamao had participated in all;
translations.idiomatic: Bamao was the emperor's own younger brother and had taken part in the Liu Shizhi and Han Zigao conspiracies;

sentences.zh: 司徒頊恐扇動中外，故以為中衛，專使之居禁中，與帝游處。

translations.literal: The prince of Ancheng Xu feared he might stir court and countryside; therefore he was made central guard commander, specifically to keep him dwelling within the forbidden quarters, associating and passing time with the emperor.
translations.idiomatic: Xu feared he might rouse court and country, and therefore made him central guard commander so he would live within the palace and keep company with the emperor.

sentences.zh: 三月，甲午，以尚書右僕射沈欽為侍中、左僕射。

translations.literal: In the third month, on jiawu, Shen Qin was made Attendant-in-Ordinary and left vice minister of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month, on jiawu, Shen Qin was made attendant-in-ordinary and left vice minister of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 夏，四月，癸丑，齊遣散騎常侍司馬幼之來聘。

translations.literal: In summer, the fourth month, on guichou, Qi sent Regular Attendant of the Scattered Riders Sima Youzhi on a friendly mission.
translations.idiomatic: In summer, the fourth month, on guichou, Northern Qi sent Regular Attendant Sima Youzhi on a friendly visit.

sentences.zh: 湘州刺史華皎聞韓子高死，內不自安，繕甲聚徒，撫循所部，啟求廣州，以卜朝廷之意。

translations.literal: Hua Jiao, governor of Xiang Province, hearing that Han Zigao had died, was ill at ease within; he repaired armor and gathered followers, caressed and comforted his jurisdiction, and memorialized requesting Guang Province to test the court's intentions.
translations.idiomatic: Hua Jiao, governor of Xiangzhou, grew uneasy when Han Zigao died; he armed his troops, rallied followers, soothed his districts, and asked for transfer to Guangzhou to probe the court.

sentences.zh: 司徒頊偽許之，而詔書未出。

translations.literal: The prince of Ancheng Xu falsely assented, but the edict had not yet been issued.
translations.idiomatic: Xu pretended to grant it, but no edict had yet been issued.

sentences.zh: 皎遣使潛引周兵，又自歸於梁，以其子玄響為質。

translations.literal: Jiao sent envoys secretly to lead Zhou troops, and himself submitted to Liang, sending his son Xuanxiang as hostage.
translations.idiomatic: Jiao secretly invited Zhou armies, submitted to the Liang, and sent his son Xuanxiang as hostage.

sentences.zh: 五月，癸巳，頊以丹楊尹吳明徹為湘州刺史。

translations.literal: On guisi, Xu made Wu Mingche governor of Xiang Province.
translations.idiomatic: On guisi, Xu appointed Wu Mingche governor of Xiangzhou.

sentences.zh: 甲午，齊以東平王儼為尚書令。

translations.literal: On jiawu, Qi made the Prince of Dongping, Yan, Minister of State Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: On jiawu, Northern Qi made Prince Dongping, Gao Yan, minister of state affairs.

sentences.zh: 司徒頊遣吳明徹帥舟師三萬趣郢州，丙申，遣征南大將軍淳於量帥舟師五萬繼之，又遣冠武將軍楊文通從安成步道出茶陵，巴山太守黃法慧從宜陽出澧陵，共襲華皎，並與江州刺史章昭達、郢州刺史程靈洗合謀進討。

translations.literal: The prince of Ancheng Xu sent Wu Mingche to lead thirty thousand men in river craft toward Ying Province; on bingshen he sent Grand General of the Southern Expedition Chunyu Liang to follow with fifty thousand; he also sent Champion Martial General Yang Wentong by the Ancheng road out through Chaling, and Huang Fahui, grand defender of Bashan, from Yiyang out through Liling—all to strike Hua Jiao jointly; they also joined plans with Zhang Zhaoda, governor of Jiang Province, and Cheng Lingxi, governor of Ying Province, to advance together in punishment.
translations.idiomatic: Xu sent Wu Mingche with thirty thousand sailors toward Yingzhou; on bingshen he dispatched Chunyu Liang the southern expedition commander with fifty thousand more; Champion Martial General Yang Wentong marched from Ancheng through Chaling, and Huang Fahui, grand defender of Bashan, from Yiyang through Liling—all converging on Hua Jiao, while Zhang Zhaoda of Jiangzhou and Cheng Lingxi of Yingzhou joined the campaign.

sentences.zh: 六月，壬寅，以司空徐度為車騎將軍，總督建康諸軍，步道趣湘州。

translations.literal: In the sixth month, on renyin, Xu made Xu Du, minister of works, grand general of chariots and cavalry, commanding all armies at Jiankang, advancing by land toward Xiang Province.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month, on renyin, Xu Du, minister of works, was made commander of all Jiankang forces and marched overland toward Xiangzhou.

sentences.zh: 辛亥，周主尊其母叱奴氏為皇太后。

translations.literal: On xinhai, the Zhou ruler honored his mother Lady Chitu as empress dowager.
translations.idiomatic: On xinhai, the Zhou ruler honored his mother Lady Chitu as empress dowager.

sentences.zh: 己未，齊封皇弟仁機為西河王，仁約為樂浪王，仁儉為穎川王，仁雅為安樂王，仁直為丹楊王，仁謙為東海王。

translations.literal: On jiwei, Qi enfeoffed his younger imperial brother Renji as Prince of Xihe, Renyao as Prince of Lelang, Renjian as Prince of Yingchuan, Renya as Prince of Anle, Renzhi as Prince of Danyang, and Renqian as Prince of Donghai.
translations.idiomatic: On jiwei, Northern Qi enfeoffed imperial brothers Renji, Renyao, Renjian, Renya, Renzhi, and Renqian as princes of Xihe, Lelang, Yingchuan, Anle, Danyang, and Donghai.

sentences.zh: 華皎使者至長安；

translations.literal: Hua Jiao's envoys reached Chang'an;
translations.idiomatic: Hua Jiao's envoys reached Chang'an;

sentences.zh: 梁王亦上書言狀，且乞師；

translations.literal: the Liang king also sent up a memorial stating the case and moreover begging troops;
translations.idiomatic: the Liang king also submitted a memorial describing the crisis and begging for troops;

sentences.zh: 周人議出師應之。

translations.literal: the Zhou men deliberated sending troops in response.
translations.idiomatic: the Zhou court debated whether to intervene.

sentences.zh: 司會崔猷曰：「前歲東征，死傷過半。

translations.literal: Vice Director Cui You said: "In years past the eastern expedition suffered casualties exceeding half.
translations.idiomatic: Vice Director Cui You said: "Our eastern campaign two years ago cost us more than half our army.

sentences.zh: 比雖循撫，瘡痍未復。

translations.literal: Though we have since comforted and tended them, the wounds are not yet healed.
translations.idiomatic: We have nursed the survivors, but the realm has not recovered.

sentences.zh: 今陳氏保境息民，共敦鄰好，豈可利其土地，納其叛臣，違盟約之信，興無名之師乎！」

translations.literal: Now the Chen house guards its borders and rests its people, both parties cultivating neighborly good faith—how can we covet their territory, receive their rebellious minister, break the faith of our alliance, and raise an unrighteous army!"
translations.idiomatic: Chen now keeps the peace at home and with us—how can we seize their land, harbor their rebel, break treaty faith, and march without just cause!"

sentences.zh: 晉公護不從。

translations.literal: Duke Hu of Jin would not follow.
translations.idiomatic: Duke Hu of Jin [Yuwen Hu] would not listen.

sentences.zh: 閏六月，戊寅，遣襄州總管衛公直督柱國陸通、大將軍田弘、權景宣、元定等將兵助之。

translations.literal: In the intercalary sixth month, on wuyin, he sent Inspector-General of Xiang Region, Duke Wei Zhi, to supervise the pillar generals Lu Tong, Grand Generals Tian Hong, Quan Jingxuan, Yuan Ding, and others to lead troops to assist them.
translations.idiomatic: In the intercalary sixth month, on wuyin, he sent Duke Wei Zhi of Xiangzhou with Generals Lu Tong, Tian Hong, Quan Jingxuan, Yuan Ding, and others to aid Jiao.

sentences.zh: 辛巳，齊左丞相咸陽武王斛律金卒，年八十。

translations.literal: On xinsi, Qi made the left chief minister, King Wu of Xianyang, Hulu Jin, die at age eighty.
translations.idiomatic: On xinsi, Northern Qi's left chief minister, King Wu of Xianyang, Hulu Jin, died at eighty.

sentences.zh: 金長子光為大將軍，次子羨及孫武都並開府儀同三司，出鎮方岳，其餘子孫封侯貴顯者眾甚。

translations.literal: Jin's eldest son Guang was grand general; his second son Xian and grandson Wudu were both commissioners with ceremonial equal to the Three Excellencies, going out to guard the frontier posts; the remaining sons and grandsons enfeoffed as marquises with noble display were very many.
translations.idiomatic: Jin's eldest son Guang was grand general; his second son Xian and grandson Wudu each held commission equal to the Three Excellencies and commanded provinces; countless kin held noble rank.

sentences.zh: 門中一皇后，二太子妃，三公主，事齊三世，貴寵無比。

translations.literal: Within the household were one empress, two crown prince consorts, three princesses; serving three generations of Qi, favor and honor were without compare.
translations.idiomatic: The clan produced one empress, two crown princesses, and three imperial princesses; through three Qi reigns their glory was unmatched.

sentences.zh: 自肅宗以來，禮敬尤重，每朝見，常聽乘步挽車至階，或以羊車迎之。

translations.literal: From Emperor Xiaozong onward ceremonial respect was especially heavy; each court audience he was often allowed to ride a hand-drawn carriage to the steps, or sometimes a sheep cart would meet him.
translations.idiomatic: Since Emperor Xiaozong's day they showed him extraordinary deference—he might ride a hand-drawn carriage to the palace steps, or be met by sheep cart.

sentences.zh: 然金不以為喜，嘗謂光曰：「我雖不讀書，聞古來外戚鮮有能保其族者。

translations.literal: Yet Jin did not take this as joy, and once told Guang: "Though I do not read books, I have heard that since antiquity maternal relatives have rarely been able to preserve their clans.
translations.idiomatic: Jin took no joy in it and once told Guang: "I may be unlettered, but I know that imperial affines seldom keep their houses standing for long.

sentences.zh: 女若有寵，為諸貴所嫉；

translations.literal: If the daughter has favor, the various nobles are jealous of her;
translations.idiomatic: If our women are favored, the nobles will envy them;

sentences.zh: 無寵，為天子所憎。

translations.literal: if she has no favor, the son of heaven detests her.
translations.idiomatic: if they lose favor, the throne will turn against them.

sentences.zh: 我家直以勳勞致富貴，何必藉女寵也！」

translations.literal: Our house has grown rich and noble purely through military merit—why must we rely on a daughter's favor!"
translations.idiomatic: Our wealth comes from battlefield merit alone—we need no daughter's grace to prosper!"

sentences.zh: 壬午，齊以東平王儼錄尚書事，以左僕射趙彥深為尚書令，數遠為左僕射，中書監徐之才為右僕射。

translations.literal: On renwu, Qi made the Prince of Dongping, Yan, concurrently recorder of the Ministry of State Affairs; Zhao Yanshen was made minister of state affairs; Shu Yuan was made left vice minister; Palace Secretariat Director Xu Zhicai was made right vice minister.
translations.idiomatic: On renwu, Northern Qi made Prince Dongping registrar of the ministry; Zhao Yanshen minister; Shu Yuan left vice minister; and director Xu Zhicai right vice minister.

sentences.zh: 定遠，昭之子也。

translations.literal: Dingyuan was the son of Zhao.
translations.idiomatic: Dingyuan was Zhao's son.

sentences.zh: 秋，七月，戊申，立皇子至澤為太子。

translations.literal: In autumn, the seventh month, on wushen, the crown prince Chize was established.
translations.idiomatic: In autumn, the seventh month, on wushen, Prince Chize was named crown prince.

sentences.zh: 八月，齊以任城王湝為太師，馮翊王潤為大司馬，段韶為左丞相，賀拔仁為右丞相，侯莫陳相為太宰，婁睿為太傅，斛律光為太保，韓祖念為大將軍，趙郡王睿為太尉，東平王儼為司徒。

translations.literal: In the eighth month Qi made the Prince of Rencheng, Hui, grand master; the Prince of Fengyi, Run, grand marshal; Duan Shao left chief minister; Heba Ren right chief minister; Hou Mo Chen Xiang grand ancestor; Lou Rui grand tutor; Hulu Guang grand guardian; Han Zunian grand general; Prince of Zhao Jun, Rui, grand minister; Prince of Dongping, Yan, minister of state.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month Northern Qi made Prince Rencheng grand master, Prince Fengyi grand marshal, and appointed Duan Shao, Heba Ren, Hou Mo Chen Xiang, Lou Rui, Hulu Guang, Han Zunian, Prince Zhao, and Prince Dongping to the highest offices.

sentences.zh: 儼有寵於上皇及胡後，時兼京畿大都督，領軍大將軍，領御史中丞。

translations.literal: Yan was favored by the retired emperor and Empress Hu; at the time he was also metropolitan commandant of the capital region, commander of the palace guard, and chief of the imperial censors.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Yan was the darling of the retired emperor and Empress Hu; he also commanded the capital garrison, the palace guard, and the censorate.

sentences.zh: 魏朝故事：中丞出，與皇太子分路，王公皆遙駐，車去牛，頓軛於地，以待其過；

translations.literal: Wei dynasty precedent: when the chief censor went out, he and the crown prince parted ways; kings and dukes all halted at a distance; teams removed the oxen, set the yoke on the ground, and awaited his passing;
translations.idiomatic: Under Wei custom, when the chief censor went abroad he took a separate route from the crown prince; princes and dukes drew aside; servants unhitched the oxen and laid the pole on the ground till he passed;

sentences.zh: 其或遲違，則前驅以赤棒棒之。

translations.literal: if they were dilatory, the advance guard would strike them with the red staff.
translations.idiomatic: laggards were struck by guards with red staffs.

sentences.zh: 自遷鄴以後，此儀廢絕，上皇欲尊寵儼，命一遵舊制。

translations.literal: Since the removal to Ye this ceremony had been abolished; the retired emperor wished to honor Yan and ordered that the old form be wholly followed.
translations.idiomatic: Since the capital moved to Ye the ritual had lapsed; the retired emperor restored it to honor Yan.

sentences.zh: 儼初從北宮出，將上中丞，凡京畿步騎、領軍官屬、中丞威儀、司徒鹵簿，莫不畢從。

translations.literal: When Yan first went out from the Northern Palace to assume the censorate, every cavalryman and infantryman of the capital command, every palace-guard officer and retainer, every piece of the censor's emblems and the minister's train—all followed without exception.
translations.idiomatic: When Yan first left the Northern Palace for his censor's rounds, the capital guard, palace commands, censorial train, and ministerial escort all turned out.

sentences.zh: 上皇與胡後張幕於華林園東門外而觀之，遣中使驟馬趣仗。

translations.literal: The retired emperor and Empress Hu spread curtains at the east gate of Hualin Garden to watch; they sent palace eunuchs galloping to hasten the guard.
translations.idiomatic: The retired emperor and the empress watched from curtains at Hualin Garden's east gate and sent eunuchs galloping to hurry his escort.

sentences.zh: 不得入，自言奉敕，赤棒應聲碎其鞍，馬驚，人墜。

translations.literal: They could not enter and claimed to bear imperial order; red staffs at once shattered the saddle; the horse bolted and the man fell.
translations.idiomatic: One party could not pass and claimed an imperial order; red staffs instantly smashed the saddle, the horse panicked, and the rider fell.

sentences.zh: 上皇大笑，以為善，更敕駐車，勞問良久。

translations.literal: The retired emperor laughed greatly, took it as excellent, again ordered the carriage to halt, and for a long while offered inquiries and praise.
translations.idiomatic: The retired emperor roared with laughter, called it splendid, had the carriage stopped, and for a long while questioned and commended him.

sentences.zh: 觀者傾鄴城。

translations.literal: The spectators filled the whole of Ye.
translations.idiomatic: The whole city turned out to watch.

sentences.zh: 儼恆在宮中，坐含光殿視事，諸父皆拜之。

translations.literal: Yan constantly remained in the palace, sitting in Hanguang Hall to conduct affairs; all his uncles bowed to him.
translations.idiomatic: Yan spent his days in the palace, holding court in Hanguang Hall while his uncles bowed to him.

sentences.zh: 上皇或時如并州，儼恆居守。

translations.literal: When the retired emperor sometimes went to Bingzhou, Yan constantly remained on guard.
translations.idiomatic: When the retired emperor went to Bingzhou, Yan stayed behind as regent.

sentences.zh: 每送行，或半路，或至晉陽乃還。

translations.literal: Each time he saw him off—sometimes halfway, sometimes only returning after reaching Jinyang.
translations.idiomatic: On each farewell he accompanied him partway—or went all the way to Jinyang before turning back.

sentences.zh: 器玩服飾，皆與齊主同，所須悉官給。

translations.literal: Utensils, toys, and dress were all the same as the Qi ruler's; whatever he needed was all supplied by the official departments.
translations.idiomatic: His furnishings and dress matched the emperor's; the ministries supplied his every need.

sentences.zh: 嘗於南宮見新冰早李，還，怒曰：「尊兄已有，我何竟無！」

translations.literal: Once at the Southern Palace he saw newly iced early plums; on returning he said in anger, "My honored elder brother already has them — why do I have none at all!"
translations.idiomatic: Once at the Southern Palace he saw newly iced early plums; on returning he said in anger, "My honored elder brother already has them — why do I have none at all!"

sentences.zh: 自是齊主或先得新奇，屬官及工人必獲罪。

translations.literal: From then on, whenever the Northern Qi ruler obtained some novelty first, the subordinate officials and craftsmen would invariably be punished.
translations.idiomatic: From then on, whenever the Northern Qi ruler obtained some novelty first, the subordinate officials and craftsmen would invariably be punished.

sentences.zh: 儼性剛決，嘗言於上皇曰：「尊兄懦，何能帥左右！」

translations.literal: Yan was bold and resolute; he once said to the retired emperor, "My honored elder brother is timid — how could he command those around him!"
translations.idiomatic: Gao Yan was bold and resolute; he once said to the retired emperor, "My honored elder brother is timid — how could he command those around him!"

sentences.zh: 上皇每稱其才，有廢立意，胡後亦勸之，既而中止。

translations.literal: The retired emperor always praised his talent and had thoughts of deposing the emperor; Empress Hu also urged it, but in the end he dropped the idea.
translations.idiomatic: The retired emperor always praised his talent and had thoughts of deposing the emperor; Empress Hu also urged it, but in the end he dropped the idea.

sentences.zh: 華皎遣使誘章昭達，昭達執送建康。

translations.literal: Hua Jiao sent an envoy to entice Zhang Zhaoda; Zhaoda seized him and sent him to Jiankang.
translations.idiomatic: Hua Jiao sent an envoy to entice Zhang Zhaoda; Zhaoda seized the envoy and sent him to Jiankang.

sentences.zh: 又誘程靈洗，靈洗斬之。

translations.literal: He also tried to entice Cheng Lingxi; Lingxi executed the envoy.
translations.idiomatic: He also tried to entice Cheng Lingxi; Lingxi beheaded the envoy.

sentences.zh: 皎以武州居其心腹，遣使旅都督陸子隆，子隆不從；

translations.literal: Jiao considered Wuzhou to lie at his very heart; he sent envoys to the itinerant grand inspector Lu Zilong, but Zilong would not obey;
translations.idiomatic: Jiao considered Wuzhou to lie at his very heart; he sent envoys to the itinerant grand inspector Lu Zilong, but Zilong refused to obey;

sentences.zh: 遣兵攻之，不克。

translations.literal: He sent troops to attack but could not take it.
translations.idiomatic: He sent troops to attack it but failed to capture it.

sentences.zh: 巴州刺史戴僧朔等並隸於皎，長沙太守曹慶等，本隸皎下，遂為之用。

translations.literal: Ba Province Inspector Dai Sengshuo and others were all subordinate to Jiao; Changsha Prefect Cao Qing and others, originally under Jiao, then served him.
translations.idiomatic: Ba Province inspector Dai Sengshuo and others were all subordinate to Jiao; Changsha prefect Cao Qing and others, who had originally served under him, now did his bidding.

sentences.zh: 司徒頊恐上流守宰皆附之，乃曲赦湘、巴二州。

translations.literal: Grand Secretary Xu feared that upstream governors and prefects would all join him, so he issued a selective amnesty for Xiang and Ba provinces.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Secretary Chen Xu feared that upstream governors and prefects would all join Jiao, so he issued a selective amnesty for Xiang and Ba provinces.

sentences.zh: 九月，乙巳，悉誅皎家屬。

translations.literal: In the ninth month, on yisi, all of Jiao's family were executed.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month, on yisi, all of Hua Jiao's family were executed.

sentences.zh: 梁以皎為司空，遣其柱國王操將兵二萬會之。

translations.literal: Liang made Jiao Minister of Works and sent its pillar of state Wang Cao to lead twenty thousand troops to join him.
translations.idiomatic: Liang made Hua Jiao minister of works and sent its pillar of state Wang Cao at the head of twenty thousand troops to join him.

sentences.zh: 周權景宣將水軍，元定將陸軍，衛公直總之，與皎俱下。

translations.literal: Northern Zhou's Quan Jingxuan commanded the navy, Yuan Ding the army, and Duke Wei Gongzhi was overall commander; they descended together with Jiao.
translations.idiomatic: Northern Zhou's Quan Jingxuan commanded the navy and Yuan Ding the army, with Duke Wei Gongzhi as overall commander; they descended together with Hua Jiao.

sentences.zh: 淳於量軍夏口，直軍魯山，使元定以步騎數千圍郢州。

translations.literal: Chunyu Liang encamped at Xiakou, Gongzhi at Lushan, and Yuan Ding was sent with several thousand foot and horse to besiege Ying Province.
translations.idiomatic: Chunyu Liang encamped at Xiakou and Gongzhi at Lushan, while Yuan Ding was sent with several thousand infantry and cavalry to besiege Ying Province.

sentences.zh: 皎軍於白螺，與吳明徹等相持。

translations.literal: Jiao encamped at Baituo and faced off against Wu Mingche and others.
translations.idiomatic: Hua Jiao encamped at Baituo and faced off against Wu Mingche and the others.

sentences.zh: 徐度、楊文通由嶺路襲湘州，盡獲其所留軍士家屬。

translations.literal: Xu Du and Yang Wentong attacked Xiang Province by the mountain route and captured all the families of the soldiers Jiao had left behind.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Du and Yang Wentong struck Xiang Province by the mountain route and captured all the families of the soldiers Hua Jiao had left behind.

sentences.zh: 皎自巴陵與周、梁水軍順流乘風而下，軍勢甚盛，戰於沌口。

translations.literal: Jiao, from Baling, with Northern Zhou and Liang navies sailed downstream with the wind; his forces were very strong, and they fought at Dunkou.
translations.idiomatic: Hua Jiao, from Baling, sailed downstream with the wind alongside the Northern Zhou and Liang navies; his forces were very strong, and the battle was joined at Dunkou.

sentences.zh: 量、明徹募軍中小艦，多賞金銀，令先出當西軍大艦受其拍；

translations.literal: Liang and Mingche recruited small boats from the army, richly rewarded them with gold and silver, and had them go out first to meet the Western army's large ships and receive their ramming attacks;
translations.idiomatic: Chunyu Liang and Wu Mingche recruited small boats from the army, richly rewarded them with gold and silver, and sent them out first to take the ramming blows of the Western army's large ships;

sentences.zh: 西軍諸艦發拍皆盡，然後量等以大艦拍之，西軍艦皆碎，沒於中流。

translations.literal: When the Western army's ships had exhausted their rams, Liang and the others used large ships to ram them; the Western army's ships were all smashed and sank midstream.
translations.idiomatic: Once the Western army's ships had exhausted their rams, Chunyu Liang and the others used large ships to ram them; the Western ships were all smashed and sank midstream.

sentences.zh: 西軍又以艦載薪，因風縱火。

translations.literal: The Western army also loaded ships with firewood and set fire with the wind.
translations.idiomatic: The Western army also loaded ships with firewood and set them ablaze with the wind.

sentences.zh: 俄而風轉，自焚，西軍大敗。

translations.literal: Shortly the wind shifted; they burned themselves, and the Western army was utterly defeated.
translations.idiomatic: Before long the wind shifted; they burned themselves, and the Western army was utterly defeated.

sentences.zh: 皎與戴僧朔單舸走，過巴陵，不敢登岸，逕奔江陵；

translations.literal: Jiao and Dai Sengshuo fled in a single boat; passing Baling they dared not land and went straight to Jiangling;
translations.idiomatic: Hua Jiao and Dai Sengshuo fled in a single boat; passing Baling they dared not go ashore and went straight to Jiangling;

sentences.zh: 衛公直亦奔江陵。

translations.literal: Duke Wei Gongzhi also fled to Jiangling.
translations.idiomatic: Duke Wei Gongzhi also fled to Jiangling.

sentences.zh: 元定孤軍，進退無路，斫竹開徑，且戰且引。

translations.literal: Yuan Ding's isolated army had no way forward or back; they cut bamboo to open a path, fighting as they withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Ding's isolated army had no way forward or back; they cut bamboo to open a path, fighting as they withdrew.

sentences.zh: 欲趣巴陵，巴陵已為徐度等所據，度等遣使偽與結盟，許縱之還國；

translations.literal: He wished to reach Baling, but Baling was already held by Xu Du and others; Du and the others sent envoys feigning an alliance and promised to let them return home;
translations.idiomatic: He tried to reach Baling, but Baling was already held by Xu Du and the others; Du sent envoys feigning an alliance and promised to let them return home;

sentences.zh: 定信之，解仗就度，度執之，盡俘其眾，並擒梁大將軍李廣。

translations.literal: Ding believed them, laid down his weapons and went to Du; Du seized him, captured his entire force, and also took Liang's grand general Li Guang.
translations.idiomatic: Ding believed them, laid down his weapons and went to Xu Du; Du seized him, captured his entire force, and also took Liang grand general Li Guang.

sentences.zh: 定憤恚而卒。

translations.literal: Ding died of rage and resentment.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Ding died of rage and resentment.

sentences.zh: 皎黨曹慶等四下餘人並伏誅。

translations.literal: Jiao's followers Cao Qing and more than forty others were all executed.
translations.idiomatic: Hua Jiao's followers Cao Qing and more than forty others were all executed.

sentences.zh: 唯以岳陽太守章昭裕，昭達之弟，桂陽太守曹宣，高祖舊臣，衡陽內史汝陰任忠，嘗有密啟，皆宥之。

translations.literal: Only Yueyang Prefect Zhang Zhaoyu, Zhaoda's younger brother; Guiyang Prefect Cao Xuan, an old minister of Emperor Gaozu; and Hengyang Administrator Ren Zhong of Runan, who had once sent secret memorials — all were spared.
translations.idiomatic: Only Yueyang prefect Zhang Zhaoyu, Zhaoda's younger brother; Guiyang prefect Cao Xuan, an old minister of Emperor Wu of Chen; and Hengyang administrator Ren Zhong of Runan, who had once sent secret memorials — all were spared.

sentences.zh: 吳明徹乘勝攻梁河東，拔之。

translations.literal: Wu Mingche pressed the victory to attack Liang's Hedong and took it.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Mingche pressed the victory to attack Liang's Hedong and captured it.

sentences.zh: 周衛公直歸罪於樑柱國殷亮；

translations.literal: Northern Zhou's Duke Wei Gongzhi blamed Liang's pillar of state Yin Liang;
translations.idiomatic: Northern Zhou's Duke Wei Gongzhi blamed Liang's pillar of state Yin Liang;

sentences.zh: 梁主知非其罪，然不敢違，遂誅之。

translations.literal: The Liang emperor knew it was not his fault, but dared not disobey, and so had him executed.
translations.idiomatic: The Liang emperor knew Yin Liang was not guilty, but dared not disobey and so had him executed.

sentences.zh: 周與陳既交惡，周沔州刺史裴寬白襄州總管，請益戍兵，並遷城於羊蹄山以避水。

translations.literal: Northern Zhou and Chen having become hostile, Zhou's Mian Province Inspector Pei Kuan informed the Xiangzhou governor-general, requesting additional garrison troops and moving the city to Mount Yangti to avoid flooding.
translations.idiomatic: Northern Zhou and Chen having become hostile, Northern Zhou's Mian Province inspector Pei Kuan informed the Xiangzhou governor-general, requesting additional garrison troops and relocating the city to Mount Yangti to avoid flooding.

sentences.zh: 總管兵未至，程靈洗舟師奄至城下。

translations.literal: Before the governor-general's troops arrived, Cheng Lingxi's naval force suddenly appeared below the walls.
translations.idiomatic: Before the governor-general's troops arrived, Cheng Lingxi's naval force suddenly appeared below the walls.

sentences.zh: 會大雨，水暴漲，靈洗引大艦臨城發拍，擊樓堞皆碎，矢石晝夜攻之三十餘日；

translations.literal: There came heavy rain and the water rose sharply; Lingxi brought large ships to the walls and launched rams, shattering the battlements; with arrows and stones they assaulted day and night for more than thirty days;
translations.idiomatic: Heavy rain came and the water rose sharply; Lingxi brought large ships to the walls and launched rams, shattering the battlements; with arrows and stones they assaulted day and night for more than thirty days;

sentences.zh: 陳人登城，寬猶帥眾執短兵拒戰；

translations.literal: Chen troops mounted the walls; Kuan still led his men with short weapons to resist;
translations.idiomatic: Chen troops mounted the walls; Pei Kuan still led his men with short weapons to resist;

sentences.zh: 又二日，乃擒之。

translations.literal: After two more days he was captured.
translations.idiomatic: After two more days he was captured.

sentences.zh: 丁巳，齊上皇如晉陽。

translations.literal: On dingsi, Northern Qi's retired emperor went to Jinyang.
translations.idiomatic: On dingsi, Northern Qi's retired emperor went to Jinyang.

sentences.zh: 山東水，饑，殭屍滿道。

translations.literal: Shandong flooded; there was famine, and corpses littered the roads.
translations.idiomatic: Shandong flooded; famine followed, and corpses littered the roads.

sentences.zh: 冬，十月，甲申，帝享太廟。

translations.literal: In winter, the tenth month, on jiashen, the emperor performed sacrifices at the imperial temple.
translations.idiomatic: In winter, the tenth month, on jiashen, the Chen emperor performed sacrifices at the imperial temple.

sentences.zh: 十一月，戊戌朔，日有食之。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month, on the first day wuxu, there was a solar eclipse.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month, on the first day wuxu, there was a solar eclipse.

sentences.zh: 丙午，齊大赦。

translations.literal: On bingwu, Northern Qi proclaimed a general amnesty.
translations.idiomatic: On bingwu, Northern Qi proclaimed a general amnesty.

sentences.zh: 癸丑，周許穆公宇文貴自突厥還，卒於張掖。

translations.literal: On guichou, Northern Zhou's Duke Mu of Xu, Yuwen Gui, returned from the Turks and died at Zhangye.
translations.idiomatic: On guichou, Northern Zhou's Duke Mu of Xu, Yuwen Gui, returned from the Turks and died at Zhangye.

sentences.zh: 齊上皇還鄴。

translations.literal: Northern Qi's retired emperor returned to Ye.
translations.idiomatic: Northern Qi's retired emperor returned to Ye.

sentences.zh: 十二月，周晉公護母卒，詔起，令視事。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, Northern Zhou Duke of Jin Yuwen Hu's mother died; an edict ordered him to leave mourning and resume duties.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month, Northern Zhou duke of Jin Yuwen Hu's mother died; an edict ordered him to leave mourning and resume his duties.

sentences.zh: 齊秘書監祖珽，與黃門侍郎劉逖友善。

translations.literal: Northern Qi Secretary Director Zu Ting was on friendly terms with Palace Attendant Liu Ti.
translations.idiomatic: Northern Qi secretary director Zu Ting was on friendly terms with palace attendant Liu Ti.

sentences.zh: 珽欲求宰相，乃疏趙彥深、元文遙、和士開罪狀，令逖奏之，逖不敢通。

translations.literal: Ting wished to become chief minister; he wrote up the crimes of Zhao Yanshen, Yuan Wenyao, and He Shikai and had Ti present the memorial, but Ti dared not pass it through.
translations.idiomatic: Zu Ting wished to become chief minister; he wrote up the crimes of Zhao Yanshen, Yuan Wenyao, and He Shikai and had Liu Ti present the memorial, but Ti dared not pass it through.

sentences.zh: 彥深等聞之，先詣上皇自陳。

translations.literal: When Yanshen and the others heard, they went first to the retired emperor and explained themselves.
translations.idiomatic: When Yanshen and the others heard of it, they went first to the retired emperor and explained themselves.

sentences.zh: 上皇大怒，執珽，詰之，珽因陳士開、文遙、彥深等朋黨、弄權、賣官、鬻獄事。

translations.literal: The retired emperor was furious; he seized Ting and interrogated him, and Ting then set forth how Shikai, Wenyao, Yanshen, and others formed factions, manipulated power, sold offices, and traded judgments.
translations.idiomatic: The retired emperor was furious; he seized Zu Ting and interrogated him, and Ting then set forth how He Shikai, Yuan Wenyao, Zhao Yanshen, and others formed factions, manipulated power, sold offices, and traded in judgments.

sentences.zh: 上皇曰：「爾乃誹謗我！」

translations.literal: The retired emperor said, "You are slandering me!"
translations.idiomatic: The retired emperor said, "You are slandering me!"

sentences.zh: 珽曰：「臣不敢誹謗，陛下取人女。」

translations.literal: Ting said, "Your subject does not dare to slander — Your Majesty takes people's daughters."
translations.idiomatic: Zu Ting said, "Your subject does not dare to slander — Your Majesty takes people's daughters."

sentences.zh: 上皇曰：「我以其饑饉，收養之耳。」

translations.literal: The retired emperor said, "I took them in because they were starving from famine, that is all."
translations.idiomatic: The retired emperor said, "I took them in because they were starving from famine, that is all."

sentences.zh: 珽曰：「何不開倉振給，乃買入後宮乎？」

translations.literal: Ting said, "Why not open the granaries and give relief — instead of buying them into the inner palace?"
translations.idiomatic: Zu Ting said, "Why not open the granaries and give relief — instead of buying them into the inner palace?"

sentences.zh: 上皇益怒，以刀環築其口，，鞭杖亂下，將撲殺之。

translations.literal: The retired emperor grew angrier still; he struck Ting's mouth with a knife ring, and lashes and cudgels rained down as he was about to beat him to death.
translations.idiomatic: The retired emperor grew angrier still; he struck Ting's mouth with a knife ring, and lashes and cudgels rained down as he was about to beat him to death.

sentences.zh: 珽呼曰：「陛下勿殺臣，臣為陛下合金丹。」

translations.literal: Ting cried out, "Your Majesty, do not kill your subject — your subject can compound golden elixir pills for Your Majesty."
translations.idiomatic: Zu Ting cried out, "Your Majesty, do not kill your subject — your subject can compound golden elixir pills for Your Majesty."

sentences.zh: 遂得少寬。

translations.literal: He was given a little respite thereby.
translations.idiomatic: He was given a little respite thereby.

sentences.zh: 珽曰：「陛下有一范增不能用。」

translations.literal: Ting said, "Your Majesty has a Fan Zeng but will not use him."
translations.idiomatic: Zu Ting said, "Your Majesty has a Fan Zeng but will not use him."

sentences.zh: 上皇又怒曰：「爾自比范增，以我為項羽邪？」

translations.literal: The retired emperor grew angry again and said, "You compare yourself to Fan Zeng and me to Xiang Yu?"
translations.idiomatic: The retired emperor grew angry again and said, "You compare yourself to Fan Zeng and me to Xiang Yu?"

sentences.zh: 珽曰：「項羽布衣，帥烏合之眾，五年而成霸業。

translations.literal: Ting said, "Xiang Yu was a commoner who led a motley crowd and in five years achieved a hegemony.
translations.idiomatic: Zu Ting said, "Xiang Yu was a commoner who led a motley crowd and in five years achieved a hegemony.

sentences.zh: 陛下藉父兄之資，才得至此，臣以為項羽未易可輕。」

translations.literal: With the resources of your father and elder brother you have only reached this point; your subject thinks Xiang Yu is not easily to be slighted."
translations.idiomatic: With the resources of your father and elder brother you have only reached this point; I think Xiang Yu is not to be slighted."

sentences.zh: 上皇愈怒，令以土塞其口。

translations.literal: The retired emperor grew still angrier and ordered earth stuffed in his mouth.
translations.idiomatic: The retired emperor grew still angrier and ordered earth stuffed in his mouth.

sentences.zh: 珽且吐且言，乃鞭二百，配甲坊，尋徙光州，敕令牢掌。

translations.literal: Ting spoke even as he spat it out; he was given two hundred lashes, assigned to the armor workshop, soon transferred to Guang Province, and ordered to be held in strict custody.
translations.idiomatic: Zu Ting spoke even as he spat it out; he was given two hundred lashes, assigned to the armor workshop, soon transferred to Guang Province, and ordered to be held in strict custody.

sentences.zh: 別駕張奉福曰：「牢者，地牢也。」

translations.literal: Assistant Administrator Zhang Fengfu said, "By 'strict custody' he means an underground dungeon."
translations.idiomatic: Assistant administrator Zhang Fengfu said, "By 'strict custody' he means an underground dungeon."

sentences.zh: 乃置地牢中，桎梏不離身；

translations.literal: So he was placed in an underground dungeon, shackles never off his body;
translations.idiomatic: So he was placed in an underground dungeon, shackles never off his body;

sentences.zh: 夜以蕪菁子為燭，眼為所熏，由是失明。

translations.literal: At night turnip seeds were used for candles; his eyes were smoked and thereby he went blind.
translations.idiomatic: At night turnip seeds were used for candles; his eyes were smoked by them and thereby he went blind.

sentences.zh: 齊七兵尚書畢義雲為治酷忍，非人理所及，於家尤甚。

translations.literal: Northern Qi's Minister of the Seven Armies Bi Yiyun in governing was cruel and ruthless beyond what human reason could accept, especially at home.
translations.idiomatic: Northern Qi's minister of the seven armies Bi Yiyun in governing was cruel and ruthless beyond what human reason could accept, especially at home.

sentences.zh: 夜為盜所殺，遺其刀，驗之，其子善昭所佩刀也。

translations.literal: At night he was killed by robbers; they left his knife — when examined, it was the knife his son Shanzhao wore.
translations.idiomatic: At night he was killed by robbers; they left his knife — when examined, it proved to be the knife his son Shanzhao wore.

sentences.zh: 有司執善昭，誅之。

translations.literal: The officials arrested Shanzhao and executed him.
translations.idiomatic: The officials arrested Shanzhao and executed him.

sentences.zh: 春，正月，己亥，安成王頊進位太傅，領司徒，加殊禮。

translations.literal: In spring, the first month, on jihai, Prince Xu of Ancheng was promoted to Grand Tutor, heading the Secretariat, with special honors.
translations.idiomatic: In spring, the first month, on jihai, Prince Xu of Ancheng, Chen Xu, was promoted to grand tutor, heading the secretariat, with special honors.

sentences.zh: 辛丑，周主祀南郊。

translations.literal: On xinchou, the Northern Zhou emperor sacrificed at the Southern Altar.
translations.idiomatic: On xinchou, the Northern Zhou emperor sacrificed at the Southern Altar.

sentences.zh: 癸亥，齊主使兼散騎常侍鄭大護來聘。

translations.literal: On guihai, Northern Qi's emperor sent Acting Regular Palace Attendant Zheng Dahu on a diplomatic mission.
translations.idiomatic: On guihai, the Northern Qi emperor sent acting regular palace attendant Zheng Dahu on a diplomatic mission.

sentences.zh: 湘東忠肅公徐度卒。

translations.literal: Duke Zhongsu of Xiangdong, Xu Du, died.
translations.idiomatic: Duke Zhongsu of Xiangdong, Xu Du, died.

sentences.zh: 二月，丁卯，周主如武功。

translations.literal: In the second month, on dingmao, the Northern Zhou emperor went to Wugong.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month, on dingmao, the Northern Zhou emperor went to Wugong.

sentences.zh: 突厥木桿可汗貳於周，更許齊人以昏，留陳公純等數年不返。

translations.literal: The Turk khagan Muhan turned disloyal to Northern Zhou, again promised marriage alliance with Northern Qi, and kept Chen Gongchun and others for years without returning them.
translations.idiomatic: The Turk khagan Muhan turned disloyal to Northern Zhou, again promised a marriage alliance with Northern Qi, and kept Chen Gongchun and others for years without returning them.

sentences.zh: 會大雷風，壞其穹廬，旬日不止。

translations.literal: There came a great thunderstorm that destroyed his yurt; for ten days it did not stop.
translations.idiomatic: There came a great thunderstorm that destroyed his yurt; for ten days it did not stop.

sentences.zh: 木桿懼，以為天譴，即備禮送其女於周，純等奉之以歸。

translations.literal: Muhan was afraid, took it as heavenly punishment, immediately prepared full rites and sent his daughter to Northern Zhou; Gongchun and the others escorted her back.
translations.idiomatic: Muhan was afraid, took it as heavenly punishment, immediately prepared full rites and sent his daughter to Northern Zhou; Chen Gongchun and the others escorted her back.

sentences.zh: 三月，癸卯，至長安，周主行親迎之禮。

translations.literal: In the third month, on guimao, they reached Chang'an; the Northern Zhou emperor performed the ceremony of greeting his bride in person.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month, on guimao, they reached Chang'an; the Northern Zhou emperor performed the ceremony of greeting his bride in person.

sentences.zh: 甲辰，周大赦。

translations.literal: On jiachen, Northern Zhou proclaimed a general amnesty.
translations.idiomatic: On jiachen, Northern Zhou proclaimed a general amnesty.

sentences.zh: 乙巳，齊以東平王儼為大將軍，南陽王綽為司徒，開府儀同三司徐顯秀為司空，廣寧王孝珩為尚書令。

translations.literal: On yisi, Northern Qi made Prince Yan of Dongping Grand General, Prince Chuo of Nanyang Grand Secretary, Xu Xianxiu of the rank of Commander-in-Chief with equal honor to the three highest offices as Minister of Works, and Prince Xiaohang of Guangning Director of the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: On yisi, Northern Qi made Prince Yan of Dongping grand general, Prince Chuo of Nanyang grand secretary, Xu Xianxiu of the rank of commander-in-chief with equal honor to the three highest offices as minister of works, and Prince Xiaohang of Guangning director of the masters of writing.

sentences.zh: 戊午，周燕文公於謹卒。

translations.literal: On wuwu, Northern Zhou's Duke Wen of Yan, Yu Jin, died.
translations.idiomatic: On wuwu, Northern Zhou's Duke Wen of Yan, Yu Jin, died.

sentences.zh: 謹勳高位重，而事上益恭，每朝參，所從不過二三騎。

translations.literal: Jin had high merit and lofty rank yet served his sovereign with growing humility; each time he attended court he brought no more than two or three mounted attendants.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Jin had high merit and lofty rank yet served his sovereign with growing humility; each time he attended court he brought no more than two or three mounted attendants.

sentences.zh: 朝廷有大事，多與謹謀之。

translations.literal: When the court had weighty matters it often consulted Jin.
translations.idiomatic: When the court had weighty matters it often consulted Yu Jin.

sentences.zh: 謹盡忠補益，於功臣中特被親信，禮遇隆重，始終無間；

translations.literal: Jin gave loyal counsel and corrective aid; among the meritorious he was uniquely trusted, honored with great ceremony from start to finish without interruption;
translations.idiomatic: Yu Jin gave loyal counsel and corrective aid; among the meritorious he was uniquely trusted, honored with great ceremony from start to finish without interruption;

sentences.zh: 教訓諸子，務存靜退，而子孫蕃衍，率皆顯達。

translations.literal: He instructed his sons to prize restraint and withdrawal, yet his descendants flourished and nearly all achieved prominence.
translations.idiomatic: He instructed his sons to prize restraint and withdrawal, yet his descendants flourished and nearly all achieved prominence.

sentences.zh: 吳明徹乘勝進攻江陵，引水灌之，梁主出頓紀南以避之。

translations.literal: Wu Mingche pressed the victory to attack Jiangling, diverting water to flood it; the Liang emperor went out and encamped at Jinan to avoid it.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Mingche pressed the victory to attack Jiangling, diverting water to flood it; the Liang emperor went out and encamped at Jinan to avoid it.

sentences.zh: 周總管田弘從梁主，副總管高琳與梁僕射王操守江陵三城，晝夜拒戰十旬。

translations.literal: Northern Zhou Governor-General Tian Hong accompanied the Liang emperor; Deputy Governor-General Gao Lin and Liang's Vice Director Wang Cao held Jiangling's three cities, resisting day and night for a hundred days.
translations.idiomatic: Northern Zhou governor-general Tian Hong accompanied the Liang emperor; deputy governor-general Gao Lin and Liang vice director Wang Cao held Jiangling's three cities, resisting day and night for a hundred days.

sentences.zh: 梁將馬武、吉徹擊明徹，敗之。

translations.literal: Liang generals Ma Wu and Ji Che struck Mingche and defeated him.
translations.idiomatic: Liang generals Ma Wu and Ji Che struck Wu Mingche and defeated him.

sentences.zh: 明徹退保公安，梁主乃得還。

translations.literal: Mingche withdrew to hold Gong'an; only then could the Liang emperor return.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Mingche withdrew to hold Gong'an; only then could the Liang emperor return.

sentences.zh: 夏，四月，辛巳，周以達奚武為太傅，尉遲迥為太保，齊公憲為大司馬。

translations.literal: In summer, the fourth month, on xinsi, Northern Zhou made Daci Wu Grand Tutor, Yuchi Jiong Grand Guardian, and Duke Qi Gongxian Grand Marshal.
translations.idiomatic: In summer, the fourth month, on xinsi, Northern Zhou made Daci Wu grand tutor, Yuchi Jiong grand guardian, and Duke of Qi Yuwen Xian grand marshal.

sentences.zh: 齊上皇如晉陽。

translations.literal: Northern Qi's retired emperor went to Jinyang.
translations.idiomatic: Northern Qi's retired emperor went to Jinyang.

sentences.zh: 齊尚書左僕射徐之才善醫，上皇有疾，之才療之，既愈，中書監和士開欲得次遷，乃出之才為兗州刺史。

translations.literal: Northern Qi's Left Vice Director of the Masters of Writing Xu Zhicai was skilled in medicine; when the retired emperor fell ill, Zhicai treated him; once cured, Chief Secretariat Director He Shikai, wanting the next promotion, had Zhicai sent out as Yan Province Inspector.
translations.idiomatic: Northern Qi's left vice director of the masters of writing Xu Zhicai was skilled in medicine; when the retired emperor fell ill, Zhicai treated him; once cured, chief secretariat director He Shikai, wanting the next promotion, had Zhicai sent out as Yan Province inspector.

sentences.zh: 五月，癸卯，以尚書右僕射胡長仁為左僕射，士開為右僕射。

translations.literal: In the fifth month, on guimao, Right Vice Director Hu Changren was made Left Vice Director, and Shikai Right Vice Director.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month, on guimao, right vice director Hu Changren was made left vice director, and He Shikai right vice director.

sentences.zh: 長仁，太上皇后之兄也。

translations.literal: Changren was the elder brother of the Grand Empress Dowager.
translations.idiomatic: Changren was the elder brother of the grand empress dowager.

sentences.zh: 庚戌，周主享太廟；

translations.literal: On gengxu, the Northern Zhou emperor performed sacrifices at the imperial temple;
translations.idiomatic: On gengxu, the Northern Zhou emperor performed sacrifices at the imperial temple;

sentences.zh: 庚申，如醴泉宮。

translations.literal: On gengshen, he went to the Liquan Palace.
translations.idiomatic: On gengshen, he went to the Liquan Palace.

sentences.zh: 壬戌，齊上皇還鄴。

translations.literal: On renxu, Northern Qi's retired emperor returned to Ye.
translations.idiomatic: On renxu, Northern Qi's retired emperor returned to Ye.

sentences.zh: 秋，七月，壬寅，周隨桓公楊忠卒，子堅襲爵。

translations.literal: In autumn, the seventh month, on renyin, Northern Zhou's Duke of Sui Yang Zhong died; his son Jian inherited the title.
translations.idiomatic: In autumn, the seventh month, on renyin, Northern Zhou's duke of Sui Yang Zhong died; his son Yang Jian inherited the title.

sentences.zh: 堅為開府儀同三司、小宮伯，晉公護欲引以為腹心。

translations.literal: Jian was Commander-in-Chief with equal honor to the three highest offices and a lesser palace baron; Duke of Jin Yuwen Hu wished to draw him in as a trusted confidant.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Jian was commander-in-chief with equal honor to the three highest offices and a lesser palace baron; duke of Jin Yuwen Hu wished to draw him in as a trusted confidant.

sentences.zh: 堅以白忠，忠曰：「兩姑之間難為婦，汝其勿往！」

translations.literal: Jian told Zhong; Zhong said, "Between two mothers-in-law it is hard to be the daughter-in-law — you had best not go!"
translations.idiomatic: Yang Jian told Zhong; Yang Zhong said, "Between two mothers-in-law it is hard to be the daughter-in-law — you had best not go!"

sentences.zh: 堅乃辭之。

translations.literal: Jian then declined.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Jian then declined.

sentences.zh: 丙午，帝享太廟。

translations.literal: On bingwu, the emperor performed sacrifices at the imperial temple.
translations.idiomatic: On bingwu, the Chen emperor performed sacrifices at the imperial temple.

sentences.zh: 戊午，周主還長安。

translations.literal: On wuwu, the Zhou ruler returned to Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: On wuwu, the Northern Zhou emperor returned to Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 壬戌，封皇弟伯智為永陽王，伯謀為桂陽王。

translations.literal: On renxu, the emperor enfeoffed his younger imperial brother Bozhi as Prince of Yongyang and Bomou as Prince of Guiyang.
translations.idiomatic: On renxu, the Chen emperor enfeoffed his younger brothers Chen Bozhi as prince of Yongyang and Chen Bomou as prince of Guiyang.

sentences.zh: 八月，齊請和於周，周遣軍司馬陸程等聘於齊；

translations.literal: In the eighth month, Qi requested peace with Zhou; Zhou sent Army Marshal Lu Cheng and others on a friendly mission to Qi;
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month, Northern Qi sought peace with Northern Zhou; Northern Zhou sent army marshal Lu Cheng and others on a diplomatic mission to Northern Qi;

sentences.zh: 九月，丙申，齊使侍中斛斯文略報之。

translations.literal: In the ninth month, on bingshen, Qi sent Palace Attendant Husiwen Lue to return the visit.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month, on bingshen, Northern Qi sent palace attendant Husiwen Lue to return the visit.

sentences.zh: 冬，十月，癸亥，周主享太廟。

translations.literal: In winter, the tenth month, on guihai, the Zhou ruler performed sacrifices at the imperial temple.
translations.idiomatic: In winter, the tenth month, on guihai, the Northern Zhou emperor performed sacrifices at the imperial temple.

sentences.zh: 庚午，帝享太廟。

translations.literal: On gengwu, the emperor performed sacrifices at the imperial temple.
translations.idiomatic: On gengwu, the Chen emperor performed sacrifices at the imperial temple.

sentences.zh: 辛巳，齊以廣寧王孝珩錄尚書事，左僕射胡長仁為尚書令，右僕射和士開為左僕射，中書監唐邕為右僕射。

translations.literal: On xinsi, Qi made Prince Guangning Xiaoheng recorder of the Department of State Affairs; Left Vice Director Hu Changren was made Director; Right Vice Director He Shikai was made Left Vice Director; Palace Secretariat Director Tang Yong was made Right Vice Director.
translations.idiomatic: On xinsi, Northern Qi made Prince Guangning Gao Xiaoxheng recorder of the Department of State Affairs; left vice director Hu Changren was made director; right vice director He Shikai was made left vice director; palace secretariat director Tang Yong was made right vice director.

sentences.zh: 十一月，壬辰朔，日有食之。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month, on the first day renchen, there was a solar eclipse.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month, on the first day renchen, there was a solar eclipse.

sentences.zh: 齊遣兼散騎常侍李諧來聘。

translations.literal: Qi sent Concurrent Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry Li Xie on a friendly mission.
translations.idiomatic: Northern Qi sent concurrent regular attendant of the scattered cavalry Li Xie on a diplomatic mission.

sentences.zh: 甲辰，周主如岐陽。

translations.literal: On jiachen, the Zhou ruler went to Qiyang.
translations.idiomatic: On jiachen, the Northern Zhou emperor went to Qiyang.

sentences.zh: 周遣開府儀同三司崔彥等聘於齊。

translations.literal: Zhou sent Commander-in-Chief of Equal Honor to the Three Highest Offices Cui Yan and others on a friendly mission to Qi.
translations.idiomatic: Northern Zhou sent commander-in-chief of equal honor to the three highest offices Cui Yan and others on a diplomatic mission to Northern Qi.

sentences.zh: 始興王伯茂以安成王頊專政，意甚不平，屢肆惡言。

translations.literal: Prince of Shixing Bamao, because the Prince of Ancheng Xu monopolized government, felt greatly resentful and repeatedly uttered malicious words.
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Shixing Chen Bamao, resentful that Prince of Ancheng Chen Xu monopolized power, repeatedly spoke ill of him.

sentences.zh: 甲寅，以太皇太后令，誣帝，雲與劉師知、華皎等通謀。

translations.literal: On jiayin, by order of the grand empress dowager, the emperor was falsely accused on the claim that he had conspired with Liu Shizhi, Hua Jiao, and others.
translations.idiomatic: On jiayin, by order of the grand empress dowager, the emperor was falsely accused of conspiring with Liu Shizhi, Hua Jiao, and others.

sentences.zh: 且曰：「文皇知子之鑒，事等帝堯；

translations.literal: And it said: "Emperor Wen's discernment in knowing his sons equaled that of Emperor Yao;
translations.idiomatic: The decree also said: "Emperor Wen's judgment in choosing his heir was like that of Emperor Yao;

sentences.zh: 傳弟之懷，又符太伯。

translations.literal: the wish to pass the throne to a younger brother also accorded with that of Taibo.
translations.idiomatic: his wish to pass the throne to a younger brother matched that of Taibo.

sentences.zh: 今可還申曩志，崇立賢君。」

translations.literal: Now we may restore and renew our former intent and install a worthy ruler on high."
translations.idiomatic: Now let us restore that original intent and enthrone a worthy ruler."

sentences.zh: 遂廢帝為臨海王，以安成王入纂。

translations.literal: Thereupon the emperor was deposed and made Prince of Linhai, and the Prince of Ancheng entered to succeed.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was then deposed as prince of Linhai, and Prince of Ancheng Chen Xu ascended the throne.

sentences.zh: 又下令，黜伯茂為溫麻侯，置諸別館，安成王使盜邀之於道，殺之車中。

translations.literal: Another order was issued deposing Bamao as Marquis of Wenma and placing him in a separate lodge; the Prince of Ancheng had bandits intercept him on the road and kill him in the carriage.
translations.idiomatic: Another order deposed Bamao as marquis of Wenma and confined him in a separate lodge; Prince of Ancheng Chen Xu had men waylay him on the road and kill him in his carriage.

sentences.zh: 齊上皇疾作，驛追徐之才，未至。

translations.literal: Northern Qi's retired emperor's illness broke out; he sent a courier post to summon Xu Zhicai, but he had not yet arrived.
translations.idiomatic: Northern Qi's retired emperor fell ill; he sent courier post to summon Xu Zhicai, but Xu had not yet arrived.

sentences.zh: 辛未，疾亟，以後事屬和士開，握其手曰：「勿負我也！」

translations.literal: On xinwei, the illness grew critical; he entrusted later affairs to He Shikai, grasped his hand, and said, "Do not fail me!"
translations.idiomatic: On xinwei, the illness grew critical; he entrusted his final affairs to He Shikai, grasped his hand, and said, "Do not disappoint me!"

sentences.zh: 遂殂於士開之手。

translations.literal: He then died in He Shikai's hands.
translations.idiomatic: He then died with He Shikai holding his hand.

sentences.zh: 明日，之才至，復遣還州。

translations.literal: The next day Xu Zhicai arrived and was sent back to his province again.
translations.idiomatic: The next day Xu Zhicai arrived and was sent back to his province.

sentences.zh: 士開秘喪三日不發。

translations.literal: He Shikai kept the death secret and did not announce the mourning for three days.
translations.idiomatic: He Shikai kept the death secret and did not announce mourning for three days.

sentences.zh: 黃門侍郎馮子琮問其故，士開曰：「神武、文襄之喪，皆秘不發。

translations.literal: Yellow Gate Gentleman Feng Zicong asked the reason; He Shikai said, "The mourning for Shenwu and Wenxiang were both kept secret and not announced.
translations.idiomatic: Yellow gate gentleman Feng Zicong asked why; He Shikai said, "The deaths of Gao Huan and Gao Cheng were both kept secret and not announced.

sentences.zh: 今至尊年少，恐王公有貳心者，意欲盡追集於涼風堂，然後與公議之。」

translations.literal: Now the emperor is young; I fear that princes and dukes with divided hearts — my intent is to summon them all to the Cool Wind Hall, and then discuss it with you, sir."
translations.idiomatic: The new emperor is young, and I worry that some princes and dukes may turn against us. I intend to summon them all to the Cool Wind Hall and then consult with you.

sentences.zh: 士開素忌太尉錄尚書事趙郡王睿及領軍婁定遠，子琮恐其矯遺詔出睿於外，奪定遠禁兵，乃說之曰：「大行先已傳位於今上，群臣富貴者，皆至尊父子之恩，但令在內貴臣一無改易，王公必無異志。

translations.literal: He Shikai had long envied Grand Commandant and Recorder of the Department of State Affairs Prince Zhao of Zhao Jun Rui and Defender-in-Chief Lou Dingyuan; Zicong feared that under a falsified deathbed testament Rui would be sent outside and Dingyuan's palace-guard troops seized, and therefore persuaded him, saying, "His late majesty had already transmitted the throne to the present emperor; among the ministers who enjoy wealth and rank, all owe their standing to the grace of the emperor and his father — if you only leave the honored ministers within unchanged, the princes and dukes will surely have no contrary intent.
translations.idiomatic: Feng Zicong feared He Shikai would use a forged deathbed testament to send Prince Zhao Rui away and seize Lou Dingyuan's palace guard. He persuaded He Shikai: "The late emperor already passed the throne to the present emperor. The ministers' wealth and rank all come from the grace of father and son — leave the inner court unchanged, and the princes will have no reason to rebel.

sentences.zh: 世異事殊，豈得與霸朝相比！

translations.literal: Times differ and affairs are not the same — how can this be compared with the founding dynasty!
translations.idiomatic: Times have changed — this is nothing like the founding era!

sentences.zh: 且公不出宮門已數日，升遐之事，行路皆傳，久而不舉，恐有他變。」

translations.literal: Moreover, sir, you have not left the palace gates for several days; news of the emperor's passing is already spreading among travelers — if the mourning is long delayed without announcement, I fear there may be other changes."
translations.idiomatic: You have not left the palace for days, and word of the emperor's death is already spreading. Delay too long and trouble may follow."

sentences.zh: 士開乃發喪。

translations.literal: He Shikai thereupon announced the mourning.
translations.idiomatic: He Shikai then announced the mourning.

sentences.zh: 丙子，大赦。

translations.literal: On bingzi, a general amnesty was proclaimed.
translations.idiomatic: On bingzi, Northern Qi proclaimed a general amnesty.

sentences.zh: 戊寅，尊太上皇后為皇太后。

translations.literal: On wuyin, the retired empress was honored as empress dowager.
translations.idiomatic: On wuyin, the retired empress was honored as empress dowager.

sentences.zh: 侍中尚書左僕射元文遙，以馮子琮，胡太后之妹夫，恐其贊太后干預朝政，與趙郡王睿、和士開謀，出子琮為鄭州刺史。

translations.literal: Palace Attendant and Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs Yuan Wenyao, because Feng Zicong was the younger sister's husband of Empress Dowager Hu and feared he would support the empress dowager in intervening in court affairs, conspired with Prince Zhao Rui and He Shikai to appoint Zicong out as prefect of Zhengzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Palace attendant and left vice director Yuan Wenyao, fearing that Feng Zicong — husband of Empress Dowager Hu's sister — would urge the empress dowager to intervene in government, conspired with Prince Zhao Rui and He Shikai to appoint Feng Zicong prefect of Zhengzhou.

sentences.zh: 世祖驕奢淫泆，役繁賦重，吏民苦之。

translations.literal: Shizu was arrogant, extravagant, and dissolute; corvée labor was frequent and taxes heavy; officials and people suffered from it.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Shizu was arrogant, extravagant, and dissolute; corvée labor was frequent and taxes heavy, and officials and commoners suffered.

sentences.zh: 甲申，詔：「所在百工細作，悉罷之。

translations.literal: On jiashen, an edict stated: "In all places, artisan fine works are all to be halted.
translations.idiomatic: On jiashen, an edict stated: "All artisan fine works everywhere are to cease.

sentences.zh: 鄴下、晉陽、中山宮人、官口之老病者，悉簡放。

translations.literal: In Ye, Jinyang, and Zhongshan, palace women and government dependents who were old or ill were all selected out and released.
translations.idiomatic: In Ye, Jinyang, and Zhongshan, elderly or sick palace women and government dependents were all released.

sentences.zh: 諸家緣坐在流所者，聽還。」

translations.literal: Among all households, those implicated by association and exiled are permitted to return."
translations.idiomatic: Those exiled through guilt by association were permitted to return home."

sentences.zh: 周梁州恆稜獠叛，總管長史南鄭趙文表討之。

translations.literal: In Zhou's Liangzhou, the Hengling Liao rebelled; the chief administrator's senior clerk of Nanzheng Zhao Wenbiao campaigned against them.
translations.idiomatic: In Northern Zhou's Liang Province, the Hengling Liao rebelled; Nanzheng chief administrator's senior clerk Zhao Wenbiao campaigned against them.

sentences.zh: 諸將欲四面進攻，文表曰：「四面攻之，獠無生路，必盡死以拒我，未易可克。

translations.literal: The generals wished to attack from all four sides; Wenbiao said, "If we attack from four sides, the Liao will have no path to life and will surely fight to the death to resist us — it will not be easy to overcome them.
translations.idiomatic: The generals wished to attack from all four sides; Zhao Wenbiao said, "If we surround them on four sides, the Liao will have no way out and will fight to the death — victory will not come easily.

sentences.zh: 今吾示以威恩，為惡者誅之，從善者撫之。

translations.literal: Now let us show them both might and mercy — punish the wicked and comfort those who follow what is good.
translations.idiomatic: Let us show both might and mercy — punish the wicked and reward those who submit.

sentences.zh: 善惡既分，破之易矣。」

translations.literal: Once good and evil are divided, breaking them will be easy."
translations.idiomatic: Once the good and the bad are separated, defeating them will be easy."

sentences.zh: 遂以此意遍令軍中。

translations.literal: He thereupon had this intent proclaimed throughout the army.
translations.idiomatic: He had this policy announced throughout the army.

sentences.zh: 時有從軍熟獠，多與恆稜親識，即以實報之。

translations.literal: At the time there were Liao in the army familiar with the region; many were personally acquainted with Hengling and reported the facts to him.
translations.idiomatic: Several Liao soldiers in the army knew Hengling personally and reported Zhao Wenbiao's plans to him.

sentences.zh: 恆稜猶豫未決，文表軍已至其境。

translations.literal: Hengling hesitated without deciding; Wenbiao's army had already reached his territory.
translations.idiomatic: Hengling hesitated, but Zhao Wenbiao's army had already reached his territory.

sentences.zh: 獠中先有二路，一平一險，有獠帥數人來請為鄉導。

translations.literal: Among the Liao there were first two routes — one level and one perilous — and several Liao chiefs came to request to serve as local guides.
translations.idiomatic: The Liao territory had two routes — one flat and one perilous — and several Liao chiefs came offering to serve as guides.

sentences.zh: 文表曰：「此路寬平，不須為導。

translations.literal: Wenbiao said, "This route is wide and level — you need not guide us.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Wenbiao said, "This route is wide and level — you need not guide us.

sentences.zh: 卿但先行好慰諭子弟，使來降也。」

translations.literal: You need only go ahead first and kindly reassure and instruct your followers to come and surrender."
translations.idiomatic: Go ahead and reassure your people — tell them to come and surrender."

sentences.zh: 乃遣之。

translations.literal: He then sent them off.
translations.idiomatic: He sent them on their way.

sentences.zh: 文表謂諸將曰：「獠帥謂吾從寬路而進，必設伏以邀我，當更出其不意。」

translations.literal: Wenbiao told the generals, "The Liao chiefs think we will advance by the broad route and will surely set an ambush to intercept us — we should strike where they do not expect."
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Wenbiao told the generals, "The Liao chiefs expect us to take the broad route and will surely ambush us there — we must strike where they do not expect."

sentences.zh: 乃引兵自狹路入，乘高而望，果有伏兵。

translations.literal: He then led troops in by the narrow route, climbed high to look, and indeed there were troops lying in ambush.
translations.idiomatic: He led his troops by the narrow route, climbed high to look, and found the ambush on the broad route.

sentences.zh: 獠既失計，爭帥眾來降。

translations.literal: The Liao, having lost their stratagem, all led their masses to come and surrender.
translations.idiomatic: The Liao, their plan foiled, surrendered en masse.

sentences.zh: 文表皆慰撫之，仍征其租稅，無敢違者。

translations.literal: Wenbiao comforted them all and yet collected their rent and taxes; none dared disobey.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Wenbiao reassured them all and then collected their taxes; none dared resist.

sentences.zh: 周人以文表為蓬州刺史。

translations.literal: Zhou appointed Wenbiao prefect of Pengzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Northern Zhou appointed Zhao Wenbiao prefect of Peng Province.

sentences.zh: 高宗宣皇帝上之上

translations.literal: High Ancestor Emperor Xuan, Part One (upper)
translations.idiomatic: The Reign of Emperor Xuan the High Ancestor, Part One

sentences.zh: 春，正月，辛卯朔，周主以齊世祖之喪罷朝會，遣司會李綸吊賻，且會葬。
