translations.literal: In spring, the first month, on the xinmao new moon, the Zhou ruler, because of Northern Qi Shizu's mourning, suspended court audiences; he sent Director of State Affairs Li Lun to offer condolences and funeral gifts, and also to attend the burial.
translations.idiomatic: In spring, the first month, on the xinmao new moon, the Northern Zhou emperor suspended court audiences for the mourning of Northern Qi's Emperor Shizu; he sent director of state affairs Li Lun to offer condolences and attend the funeral.

sentences.zh: 甲午，安成王即皇帝位，改元，大赦。

translations.literal: On jiawu, the Prince of Ancheng ascended the imperial throne, changed the era name, and proclaimed a general amnesty.
translations.idiomatic: On jiawu, Prince of Ancheng Chen Xu ascended the throne, changed the era name, and proclaimed a general amnesty.

sentences.zh: 復太皇太后為皇太后，皇太后為文皇后；

translations.literal: The grand empress dowager was restored as empress dowager, and the empress dowager was made Empress Wen;
translations.idiomatic: The grand empress dowager was restored as empress dowager, and the empress dowager was titled Empress Wen;

sentences.zh: 立妃柳氏為皇后，世子叔寶為太子；

translations.literal: Consort Lady Liu was installed as empress, and the heir Shubao was made crown prince;
translations.idiomatic: Consort Liu was installed as empress, and the heir Chen Shubao was made crown prince;

sentences.zh: 封皇子叔陵為始興王，奉昭烈王祀。

translations.literal: The imperial son Shuling was enfeoffed as Prince of Shixing, to maintain the sacrifices for Prince Zhaolie.
translations.idiomatic: The prince Chen Shuling was enfeoffed as prince of Shixing to maintain the cult of Prince Zhaolie.

sentences.zh: 乙未，上謁太廟。

translations.literal: On yiwei, the emperor paid reverence at the imperial temple.
translations.idiomatic: On yiwei, Emperor Chen Xu paid reverence at the imperial temple.

sentences.zh: 丁酉，以尚書僕射沈欽為左僕射，度支尚書王勱為右僕射。

translations.literal: On dingyou, Minister of the Ministry Shen Qin was made left vice director, and Minister of the Revenues Bureau Wang Mai was made right vice director.
translations.idiomatic: On dingyou, minister Shen Qin was made left vice director and minister of revenues Wang Mai right vice director.

sentences.zh: 勱，份之孫也。

translations.literal: Mai was the grandson of Fen.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Mai was the grandson of Wang Fen.

sentences.zh: 辛丑，上祀南郊。

translations.literal: On xinchou, the emperor sacrificed at the southern suburb.
translations.idiomatic: On xinchou, Emperor Chen Xu sacrificed at the southern suburb.

sentences.zh: 壬寅，封皇子叔英為豫章王，叔堅為長沙王。

translations.literal: On renyin, the imperial sons Shuying and Shujian were enfeoffed as Prince of Yuzhang and Prince of Changsha.
translations.idiomatic: On renyin, Prince Chen Shuying was enfeoffed as prince of Yuzhang and Chen Shujian as prince of Changsha.

sentences.zh: 戊午，上享太廟。

translations.literal: On wuwu, the emperor performed sacrifices at the imperial temple.
translations.idiomatic: On wuwu, Emperor Chen Xu performed sacrifices at the imperial temple.

sentences.zh: 齊博陵文簡王濟，世祖之母弟也，為定州刺史，語人曰：「次敘當至我矣。」

translations.literal: Northern Qi's Prince Wen of Boling Ji, Shizu's younger brother by the same mother, was prefect of Dingzhou; he told people, "By order of succession it ought soon to come to me."
translations.idiomatic: Northern Qi's Prince Wenjian of Boling Gao Ji, the retired emperor's full younger brother, was prefect of Dingzhou; he told people, "By order of succession, the throne should next come to me."

sentences.zh: 齊主聞之，陰使人就州殺之，葬贈如禮。

translations.literal: When the Qi ruler heard this, he secretly sent men to the province to kill him; burial honors and gifts were given according to rites.
translations.idiomatic: When the Northern Qi emperor heard this, he secretly sent men to the province to kill him, then buried him with the honors due a prince.

sentences.zh: 二月，乙亥，上耕藉田。

translations.literal: In the second month, on yihai, the emperor plowed the sacred field.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month, on yihai, Emperor Chen Xu plowed the sacred field.

sentences.zh: 甲申，齊葬武成帝於永平陵，廟號世祖。

translations.literal: On jiashen, Qi buried Wucheng Di at Yongping Mausoleum; the temple name was Shizu.
translations.idiomatic: On jiashen, Northern Qi buried Retired Emperor Wucheng at Yongping Mausoleum with the temple name Shizu.

sentences.zh: 己丑，齊徙東平王儼為琅邪王。

translations.literal: On jichou, Qi transferred the Prince of Dongping Yan to be Prince of Langye.
translations.idiomatic: On jichou, Northern Qi transferred Prince Dongping Gao Yan to prince of Langye.

sentences.zh: 齊遣侍中叱列長叉聘於周。

translations.literal: Qi sent Palace Attendant Chilie Changcha on a friendly mission to Zhou.
translations.idiomatic: Northern Qi sent palace attendant Chilie Changcha on a diplomatic mission to Northern Zhou.

sentences.zh: 齊以司空徐顯秀為太尉，並省尚書令婁定遠為司空。

translations.literal: Qi made Minister of Works Xu Xianxiu grand commandant, and Concurrent Director of the Department of State Affairs Lou Dingyuan minister of works.
translations.idiomatic: Northern Qi made minister of works Xu Xianxiu grand commandant and concurrent director Lou Dingyuan minister of works.

sentences.zh: 初，侍中、尚書右僕射和士開，為世祖所親狎，出入臥內，無復期度，遂得幸於胡後。

translations.literal: Initially, Palace Attendant and Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs He Shikai, being intimate with Shizu, entered and left the inner sleeping quarters without further propriety, and thereby gained favor with Empress Hu.
translations.idiomatic: Initially, palace attendant and right vice director He Shikai was so intimate with Retired Emperor Shizu that he freely entered the inner chambers, and thereby gained Empress Hu's favor.

sentences.zh: 及世祖殂，齊主以士開受顧托，深委任之，威權益盛；

translations.literal: When Shizu died, the Qi ruler, because He Shikai had received his deathbed entrustment, deeply relied on and entrusted him; his power and authority grew ever greater;
translations.idiomatic: When Shizu died, the Northern Qi emperor, believing He Shikai had received the late emperor's deathbed trust, relied on him heavily, and He Shikai's power grew;

sentences.zh: 與婁定遠及錄尚書事趙彥深、侍中尚書左僕射元文遙、開府儀同三司唐邕、領軍綦連猛、高阿那肱、度支尚書胡長粲俱用事，時號「八貴」。

translations.literal: Together with Lou Dingyuan and Recorder Zhao Yanshen, Palace Attendant and Left Vice Director Yuan Wenyao, Commander-in-Chief of Equal Honor Tang Yong, Defender-in-Chief Qilian Meng, Gao Anagou, and Minister of Revenues Hu Changcan, they all held power; at the time they were called the "Eight Worthies."
translations.idiomatic: Together with Lou Dingyuan, recorder Zhao Yanshen, palace attendant and left vice director Yuan Wenyao, commander-in-chief Tang Yong, defender-in-chief Qilian Meng, Gao Anagou, and minister of revenues Hu Changcan, they all wielded power and were called the "Eight Worthies."

sentences.zh: 太尉趙郡王睿、大司馬馮翊王潤、安德王延宗與婁定遠、元文遙皆言開齊主，請出士開為外任。

translations.literal: Grand Commandant Prince Zhao Rui, Grand Marshal Prince of Fengyi Run, Prince Ande Yanzong together with Lou Dingyuan and Yuan Wenyao all spoke to open access to the Qi ruler and requested that He Shikai be sent out to an external post.
translations.idiomatic: Grand commandant Prince Zhao Rui, grand marshal Prince Fengyi Gao Run, Prince Ande Gao Yanzong, Lou Dingyuan, and Yuan Wenyao all petitioned the emperor to send He Shikai to a provincial post.

sentences.zh: 會胡太后觴朝貴於前殿，睿面陳士開罪失云：「士開先帝弄臣，城狐社鼠，受納貨賂，穢亂宮掖。

translations.literal: When Empress Dowager Hu feasted the court nobles in the forward hall, Rui stated He Shikai's offenses to his face, saying: "He Shikai was the late emperor's favorite minion, a vermin of palace walls and temple soil; he accepted bribes and befouled the inner palace.
translations.idiomatic: When Empress Dowager Hu feasted the court nobles in the front hall, Rui publicly accused He Shikai: "He Shikai was the late emperor's favorite minion, a vermin of court and altar; he took bribes and defiled the inner palace.

sentences.zh: 臣等義無杜口，冒死陳之。」

translations.literal: We ministers, by right, cannot keep silent — we risk death to state this."
translations.idiomatic: We cannot in conscience stay silent — we speak even at the risk of our lives."

sentences.zh: 太后曰：「先帝在時，王等何不言！

translations.literal: The empress dowager said: "When the late emperor was alive, why did you princes not speak!
translations.idiomatic: The empress dowager said: "When the late emperor was alive, why did you not speak then!

sentences.zh: 今欲欺孤寡邪？

translations.literal: Do you now wish to deceive the orphaned and the widowed?
translations.idiomatic: Do you now mean to bully a widow and a young emperor?

sentences.zh: 且飲酒，勿多言！」

translations.literal: Moreover, drink wine — speak no more!"
translations.idiomatic: Drink your wine and say no more!"

sentences.zh: 睿等詞色愈厲。

translations.literal: Rui and the others grew ever fiercer in word and countenance.
translations.idiomatic: Rui and the others grew ever more vehement.

sentences.zh: 儀同三司安吐根曰：「臣本商胡，得在諸貴行末，既受厚恩，豈敢惜死！

translations.literal: Commander-in-Chief of Equal Honor Antugen said: "I am originally a merchant Hu; to be at the end of the ranks of the nobles, and yet have received thick favor — how would I dare spare death!
translations.idiomatic: Commander-in-chief of equal honor Antugen said: "I am but a merchant of Hu origin, placed among the nobles only by your grace — how can I fear death!

sentences.zh: 不出士開，朝野不定。」

translations.literal: If He Shikai is not removed, court and countryside will not be settled."
translations.idiomatic: Unless He Shikai is removed, court and realm will know no peace."

sentences.zh: 太后曰：「異日論之，王等且散！」

translations.literal: The empress dowager said: "Let us discuss this another day — you princes may disperse!"
translations.idiomatic: The empress dowager said: "We shall discuss this another day — you may all withdraw!"

sentences.zh: 睿等或投冠於地，或拂衣而起。

translations.literal: Rui and the others either threw their caps to the ground or shook out their robes and rose.
translations.idiomatic: Some of them threw their caps to the floor; others rose and swept out their robes.

sentences.zh: 明日，睿等復詣雲龍門，令文遙入奏之，三返，太后不聽。

translations.literal: The next day Rui and the others again went to the Cloud Dragon Gate; they had Wenyao enter to memorialize — three times he returned; the empress dowager would not listen.
translations.idiomatic: The next day they went again to the Cloud Dragon Gate and had Yuan Wenyao memorialize three times; the empress dowager refused to hear them.

sentences.zh: 左丞相段韶使胡長粲傳太后言曰：「梓宮在殯，事太忽忽，欲王等更思之！」

translations.literal: Left Chancellor Duan Shao had Hu Changcan transmit the empress dowager's words, saying: "The imperial coffin is still in mourning hall — affairs are too hurried; I wish you princes to reconsider!"
translations.idiomatic: Left chancellor Duan Shao had Hu Changcan relay the empress dowager's message: "The emperor's coffin still lies in state and matters are too urgent — I wish you would reconsider!"

sentences.zh: 睿等遂皆拜謝。

translations.literal: Rui and the others thereupon all bowed and thanked her.
translations.idiomatic: Rui and the others bowed and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 長粲覆命，太后曰：「成妹母子家者，兄之力也。」

translations.literal: Changcan reported back; the empress dowager said: "To make Sister's house into a mother-and-son household was elder brother's power."
translations.idiomatic: When Changcan reported back, the empress dowager said: "It was your elder brother's doing that made me empress and my son emperor."

sentences.zh: 厚賜睿等，罷之。

translations.literal: She richly rewarded Rui and the others and dismissed them.
translations.idiomatic: She richly rewarded Rui and the others and dismissed them.

sentences.zh: 太后及齊主召問士開，對曰：「先帝於群臣之中，待臣最厚。

translations.literal: The empress dowager and the Qi ruler summoned He Shikai to question him; he replied: "Among all the ministers, the late emperor treated me most generously.
translations.idiomatic: The empress dowager and the Northern Qi emperor summoned He Shikai and questioned him; he replied: "Among all the ministers, the late emperor treated me most generously.

sentences.zh: 陛下諒暗始爾，大臣皆有覬覦。

translations.literal: Your majesty's mourning has only just begun; the great ministers all harbor covetous designs.
translations.idiomatic: Your majesty's mourning has only just begun, and the great ministers are already scheming.

sentences.zh: 今若出臣，正是剪陛下羽翼。

translations.literal: If you now remove me, that is precisely to clip your majesty's wings.
translations.idiomatic: If you send me away now, you will only be cutting away your own wings.

sentences.zh: 宜謂睿等云：『文遙與臣，俱受先帝任用，豈可一去一留！

translations.literal: You ought to tell Rui and the others: 'Wenyao and I both received appointment by the late emperor — how can one go and one stay!
translations.idiomatic: Tell Rui and the others: 'Yuan Wenyao and I were both appointed by the late emperor — how can one be sent away while the other remains!

sentences.zh: 並可用為州，且出納如舊。

translations.literal: Both may be used as prefects of provinces, and revenue and expenditure as before.
translations.idiomatic: Send us both to provincial posts, but let us continue handling revenues as before.

sentences.zh: 待過山陵，然後遣之。』

translations.literal: Wait until after the imperial tomb rites, and then send us away.'
translations.idiomatic: Wait until after the burial rites, and then dispatch us.'

sentences.zh: 睿等謂臣真出，心必喜之。」

translations.literal: Rui and the others, thinking I am truly being sent out, in their hearts will surely rejoice."
translations.idiomatic: Rui and the others will think you are really sending me away and will surely be pleased."

sentences.zh: 帝及太后然之，告睿等如其言。

translations.literal: The emperor and empress dowager assented; they told Rui and the others according to his words.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor and empress dowager agreed and told Rui and the others as he advised.

sentences.zh: 乃以土開為兗州刺史，文遙為西兗州刺吏。

translations.literal: Thereupon Shikai was made inspector of Yan Province, and Wenyao inspector of West Yan Province.
translations.idiomatic: He Shikai was appointed inspector of Yan Province and Yuan Wenyao inspector of West Yan Province.

sentences.zh: 葬畢，等睿促士開就路。

translations.literal: When the burial was complete, Rui and the others urged Shikai to set out on the road.
translations.idiomatic: After the burial rites were finished, Lou Rui and the others pressed He Shikai to depart.

sentences.zh: 太后欲留士開過百日，睿不許；

translations.literal: The empress dowager wished to keep Shikai beyond the hundredth day; Rui would not permit it;
translations.idiomatic: The empress dowager wanted to keep He Shikai past the hundredth day of mourning, but Lou Rui refused;

sentences.zh: 數日之內，太后數以為言。

translations.literal: Within several days, the empress dowager repeatedly spoke of it.
translations.idiomatic: Within a few days the empress dowager brought it up again and again.

sentences.zh: 有中人知太后密旨者。

translations.literal: There was a palace eunuch who knew the empress dowager's secret intent.
translations.idiomatic: There was a palace eunuch who knew the empress dowager's private wishes.

sentences.zh: 謂睿曰：「太后意既如此，殿下何宜苦違！」

translations.literal: said to Rui: "Since the empress dowager's intent is already thus, Your Highness, why should you stubbornly oppose it!"
translations.idiomatic: He said to Lou Rui: "The empress dowager's mind is set — why must Your Highness resist so hard!"

sentences.zh: 睿曰：「吾受委不輕。

translations.literal: Rui said: "The commission I received is no light matter.
translations.idiomatic: Lou Rui said: "The charge entrusted to me is no small thing.

sentences.zh: 今嗣主幼沖，豈可使邪臣在側！

translations.literal: The succeeding ruler is young and tender — how can a wicked minister be allowed at his side!
translations.idiomatic: The new emperor is still a child — how can I let a corrupt minister remain at his side!

sentences.zh: 不守之以死，何面戴天！」

translations.literal: If I do not guard against this unto death, what face have I to bear up under Heaven!"
translations.idiomatic: If I do not defend this unto death, what face could I show beneath Heaven!"

sentences.zh: 遂更見太后，苦言之。

translations.literal: He thereupon went again to see the empress dowager and pleaded bitterly.
translations.idiomatic: He went again to the empress dowager and pleaded with her at length.

sentences.zh: 太后令酌酒賜睿，睿正色曰：「今論國家大事，非為卮酒！」

translations.literal: The empress dowager ordered wine poured and bestowed on Rui; Rui, with stern countenance, said: "We are now discussing great affairs of state — this is not for a cup of wine!"
translations.idiomatic: The empress dowager had wine poured and offered it to Lou Rui; he said gravely: "We are discussing the fate of the realm — this is no time for a cup of wine!"

sentences.zh: 言訖，遽出。

translations.literal: When he had finished speaking, he hurried out.
translations.idiomatic: With that he rose and left at once.

sentences.zh: 士開載美女珠簾詣婁定遠，謝曰：「諸貴欲殺士開，蒙王力，特全其命，用為方伯。

translations.literal: Shikai loaded beautiful women and a pearl curtain and went to Lou Dingyuan, apologizing: "The great nobles wished to kill Shikai; by the king's power my life was specially preserved, and I was made a regional inspector.
translations.idiomatic: He Shikai went to Lou Dingyuan bearing beautiful women and a pearl curtain and said: "The great nobles wanted me dead; only by Your Majesty's grace was my life spared and I was sent to govern a province.

sentences.zh: 今當奉別，謹上二女子、一珠簾。」

translations.literal: Now as I take my leave, I respectfully present two women and one pearl curtain."
translations.idiomatic: As I take my leave, I humbly offer two women and a pearl curtain."

sentences.zh: 定遠喜，謂士開曰：「欲還入不？」

translations.literal: Dingyuan was pleased and said to Shikai: "Do you wish to return inside?"
translations.idiomatic: Dingyuan was delighted and asked He Shikai: "Do you want to go back to court?"

sentences.zh: 士開曰：「在內久不自安，今得出，實遂本志，不願更入。

translations.literal: Shikai said: "Within the palace I long felt ill at ease; now that I can go out, I have truly fulfilled my original wish and do not wish to enter again.
translations.idiomatic: He Shikai said: "I never felt secure at court; now that I am free to leave, I have what I wanted and have no wish to return.

sentences.zh: 但乞王保護，長為大州刺史足矣。」

translations.literal: I only beg the king's protection — to remain a great provincial inspector forever is enough."
translations.idiomatic: I ask only that Your Majesty protect me — to serve as inspector of a great province for the rest of my days would be enough."

sentences.zh: 定遠信之。

translations.literal: Dingyuan believed him.
translations.idiomatic: Dingyuan believed him.

sentences.zh: 送至門，士開曰：「今當遠出，願得一辭覲二宮。」

translations.literal: Seeing him to the gate, Shikai said: "Now that I am going far away, I wish to obtain one farewell audience with the two palaces."
translations.idiomatic: At the gate He Shikai said: "I am about to depart for a distant post; may I have one farewell audience with the empress dowager and the emperor?"

sentences.zh: 定遠許之。

translations.literal: Dingyuan granted it.
translations.idiomatic: Dingyuan agreed.

sentences.zh: 士開由是得見太后及帝，進說曰：「先帝一旦登遐，臣愧不能自死。

translations.literal: Shikai thereby obtained an audience with the empress dowager and the emperor, and advancing his plea said: "When the late emperor suddenly ascended to the far shore, I was ashamed that I could not die with him.
translations.idiomatic: Thus He Shikai gained an audience with the empress dowager and the emperor and said: "When the late emperor died so suddenly, I was ashamed that I did not follow him in death.

sentences.zh: 觀朝貴意勢，欲以陛下為乾明。

translations.literal: Observing the intent and power of the court nobles, they wish to make Your Majesty like Ganming.
translations.idiomatic: Looking at the power of the court nobles, they mean to treat Your Majesty as they did Ganming.

sentences.zh: 臣出之後，必有大變，臣何面目見先帝於地下！」

translations.literal: After I go out, there will surely be a great upheaval — what face have I to meet the late emperor under the earth!"
translations.idiomatic: Once I am sent away, disaster will surely follow — what face could I show the late emperor in the grave!"

sentences.zh: 因慟哭。

translations.literal: He thereupon wailed in grief.
translations.idiomatic: He broke into loud weeping.

sentences.zh: 帝、太后皆泣，問：「計安出？」

translations.literal: The emperor and empress dowager both wept and asked: "What plan do you propose?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor and empress dowager wept and asked: "What is to be done?"

sentences.zh: 士開曰：「臣已得入，復何所慮，正須數行詔書耳。」

translations.literal: Shikai said: "I have already gained entry — what is there left to worry about? One need only issue a few lines of edict."
translations.idiomatic: He Shikai said: "I am already inside — what is there to fear? A few edicts will suffice."

sentences.zh: 於是詔出定遠為青州刺史，責趙郡王珽以不臣之罪。

translations.literal: Thereupon an edict sent Dingyuan out as inspector of Qing Province and charged Prince of Zhao, Ting, with the crime of disloyalty.
translations.idiomatic: Edicts then sent Lou Dingyuan to Qing Province as inspector and charged Prince Zhao with treason.

sentences.zh: 旦日，睿將復入諫，妻子鹹止之，睿曰：「社稷事重，吾寧死事先皇，不忍見朝廷顛沛。」

translations.literal: The next morning Rui was about to enter again to remonstrate; his wife and children all tried to stop him. Rui said: "The altars of state are weighty — I would rather die serving the late emperor than live to see the court thrown into turmoil."
translations.idiomatic: The next day Lou Rui prepared to remonstrate again; his wife and children all tried to stop him. He said: "The realm comes first — I would rather die serving the late emperor than watch the court collapse."

sentences.zh: 至殿門，又有人謂曰：「殿下勿入，恐有變。」

translations.literal: Reaching the palace gate, someone again said: "Your Highness, do not enter — I fear there may be trouble."
translations.idiomatic: At the palace gate someone warned him: "Do not go in, Your Highness — there may be danger."

sentences.zh: 睿曰：「吾上不負天，死亦無恨。」

translations.literal: Rui said: "Above I owe Heaven no debt — even in death I shall have no regret."
translations.idiomatic: Lou Rui said: "I have done nothing to shame Heaven — I can die without regret."

sentences.zh: 入，見太后，太后復以為言，睿執之彌固。

translations.literal: He entered and saw the empress dowager; she again spoke as before, and Rui held to his position all the firmer.
translations.idiomatic: He went in to see the empress dowager; she repeated her arguments, but Lou Rui held all the more firmly to his stand.

sentences.zh: 出，至永巷，遇兵，執送華林園雀離佛院，令劉桃枝拉殺之。

translations.literal: Coming out, at the Eternal Lane he met soldiers, who seized him and sent him to the Sparrow-Departing Buddha Hall in Hualin Garden, where Liu Taozhi was ordered to strangle him to death.
translations.idiomatic: On his way out, at Eternal Lane, he met soldiers who seized him and took him to the Sparrow-Departing Buddha Hall in Hualin Garden, where Liu Taozhi strangled him.

sentences.zh: 睿久典朝廷，清正自守，朝野冤惜之。

translations.literal: Rui had long presided over the court, upright and self-restrained; court and countryside alike grieved at the injustice.
translations.idiomatic: Lou Rui had long governed the court with integrity; officials and commoners alike mourned his unjust death.

sentences.zh: 復以士開為侍中、尚書左僕射。

translations.literal: Shikai was again made palace attendant and left vice director of the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: He Shikai was restored as palace attendant and left vice director of the Masters of Writing.

sentences.zh: 定遠歸士開所遺，加以餘珍賂之。

translations.literal: Dingyuan returned what Shikai had given him and added other rare gifts to bribe him.
translations.idiomatic: Lou Dingyuan returned He Shikai's gifts and added more treasures as a bribe.

sentences.zh: 三月，齊王如晉陽。

translations.literal: In the third month the Qi ruler went to Jinyang.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month the Northern Qi emperor went to Jinyang.

sentences.zh: 夏，四月，甲子，以并州尚書省為大基聖寺，晉祠為大崇皇寺。

translations.literal: In summer, the fourth month, on jiazi, the Masters of Writing office of Bing Province was made the Great Foundation Sacred Temple, and the Jin Shrine the Great August Imperial Temple.
translations.idiomatic: In summer, the fourth month, on jiazi, the provincial secretariat of Bingzhou was converted into the Great Foundation Sacred Temple and the Jin Shrine into the Great August Imperial Temple.

sentences.zh: 乙丑，齊主還鄴。

translations.literal: On yichou the Qi ruler returned to Ye.
translations.idiomatic: On yichou the Northern Qi emperor returned to Ye.

sentences.zh: 齊主年少，多嬖寵。

translations.literal: The Qi ruler was young and had many favorites.
translations.idiomatic: The Northern Qi emperor was young and kept many favorites.

sentences.zh: 武衛將軍高阿那肱，素以諂佞為世祖琢和士開所厚，世祖多令在東宮侍齊主，由是有寵，累遷並省尚書令，封淮陰王。

translations.literal: Martial Guard General Gao Anaguh had long relied on flattery and was favored by Emperor Shizu and He Shikai; Shizu often had him attend the Qi ruler in the Eastern Palace, and by this he gained favor, rising repeatedly to become chief of the Bing provincial secretariat and was enfeoffed as Prince of Huaiyin.
translations.idiomatic: Martial guard general Gao Anaguh had long lived by flattery and was favored by Emperor Shizu and He Shikai; Shizu often posted him in the Eastern Palace to attend the young emperor, and through this he rose to chief of the Bing provincial secretariat and was enfeoffed as prince of Huaiyin.

sentences.zh: 世祖簡都督二十人，使侍衛東宮，昌黎韓長鸞預焉，齊主獨親愛長鸞。

translations.literal: Emperor Shizu selected twenty commanders to guard the Eastern Palace; Han Changluan of Changli was among them, and the Qi ruler alone cherished Changluan.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Shizu chose twenty commanders to guard the Eastern Palace; Han Changluan of Changli was among them, and the young emperor favored Changluan above the rest.

sentences.zh: 長鸞名鳳，以字行，累遷侍中、領軍，總知內省機密。

translations.literal: Changluan's given name was Feng; he went by his style, rising repeatedly to palace attendant and commander of the guards, and oversaw the inner court's secret affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Changluan's given name was Feng, but he was known by his style; he rose to palace attendant and commander of the guards and controlled the inner court's secrets.

sentences.zh: 宮婢陸令萱者，其夫漢陽駱超，坐謀叛誅，令萱配掖庭，子提婆，亦沒為奴。

translations.literal: There was a palace maid, Lu Lingxuan; her husband Luo Chao of Hanyang was executed for plotting rebellion; Lingxuan was assigned to the rear palace, and her son Tipo was also enslaved.
translations.idiomatic: There was a palace woman named Lu Lingxuan; her husband Luo Chao of Hanyang was executed for treason, Lingxuan was sent to the rear palace, and her son Tipo was enslaved as well.

sentences.zh: 齊王之在襁褓，令萱保養之。

translations.literal: When the Qi ruler was in swaddling clothes, Lingxuan nursed and raised him.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Lingxuan had nursed the future emperor from infancy.

sentences.zh: 令萱巧黠，善取媚，有寵於胡太后，宮掖之中，獨擅威福，封為郡君，和士開、高阿那肱皆為之養子。

translations.literal: Lingxuan was clever and cunning, skilled at winning favor; she had the empress dowager Hu's affection and alone wielded power and privilege within the palace; she was enfeoffed as a district lady, and He Shikai and Gao Anaguh both became her adopted sons.
translations.idiomatic: Clever and skilled at flattery, she won the favor of Empress Dowager Hu and ruled the inner palace alone; she was enfeoffed as a district lady, and He Shikai and Gao Anaguh became her adopted sons.

sentences.zh: 齊主以令萱為女侍中。

translations.literal: The Qi ruler made Lingxuan a female palace attendant.
translations.idiomatic: The Northern Qi emperor made Lu Lingxuan a female palace attendant.

sentences.zh: 令萱引提婆入侍齊主，朝夕戲狎，累遷至開府儀同三司、虎衛大將軍。

translations.literal: Lingxuan brought Tipo in to attend the Qi ruler; day and night they frolicked together, and he rose repeatedly to grand master with the same ceremonial as the Three Excellencies and great general of the Tiger Guard.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Lingxuan brought Tipo into the emperor's service; they played together day and night, and Tipo rose to grand master of the first rank and great general of the Tiger Guard.

sentences.zh: 宮人穆捨利者，斛律後之從婢也，有寵於齊王；

translations.literal: There was a palace woman, Mu Sheli, a cousin-servant of Lady Hulu; she had the Qi ruler's favor;
translations.idiomatic: There was a palace woman, Mu Sheli, a cousin of Lady Hulu's who served in the palace and had won the emperor's favor;

sentences.zh: 令萱欲附之，乃為之養母，薦為弘德夫人，因令提婆冒姓穆氏。

translations.literal: Lingxuan wished to attach herself to her, and so became her adoptive mother, recommended her as Lady of Promoting Virtue, and had Tipo take the surname Mu.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Lingxuan sought her patronage, adopted her as a daughter, had her made Lady of Promoting Virtue, and had Tipo take the surname Mu.

sentences.zh: 然和士開用事最久，諸幸臣皆依附之，以固其寵。

translations.literal: Yet He Shikai had held power longest; all the favored ministers attached themselves to him to secure their favor.
translations.idiomatic: Yet He Shikai had held power longest, and all the emperor's favorites clung to him to keep their place.

sentences.zh: 齊主思祖珽，就流囚中除海州刺史。

translations.literal: The Qi ruler thought of Zu Ting and, from among the exiled prisoners, appointed him inspector of Hai Province.
translations.idiomatic: The Northern Qi emperor recalled Zu Ting and appointed him inspector of Haizhou while he was still in exile.

sentences.zh: 珽乃遺陸媼弟儀同三司悉達書曰：「趙彥深心腹陰沉，欲行伊、霍事，儀同姊弟豈得平安，何不早用智士邪！」

translations.literal: Ting then sent a letter to Lu Lingxuan's younger brother, Grand Master of the First Rank Xida, saying: "Zhao Yanshen is deep-scheming at heart; he wishes to perform an Yi-Yin, Huo Guang deed — can the grand master's brother and sister remain safe? Why not employ a wise man early!"
translations.idiomatic: Zu Ting wrote to Lu Lingxuan's brother Xida, a grand master of the first rank: "Zhao Yanshen is secretly plotting regency like Yi Yin and Huo Guang — can you and your sister remain safe? Why not bring in a clever man now!"

sentences.zh: 和士開亦以珽有膽略，欲引為謀主，乃棄舊怨，虛心待之，與陸媼言於帝曰：「襄、宣、昭三帝之子，皆不得立。

translations.literal: He Shikai also, seeing that Ting had courage and strategy, wished to draw him in as chief strategist; he therefore set aside old grudges and received him with an open mind, and together with Lu Lingxuan spoke to the emperor: "The sons of the three emperors Xiang, Xuan, and Zhao were none able to ascend the throne.
translations.idiomatic: He Shikai too saw that Zu Ting had nerve and wit and wanted him as a strategist; he put aside old enmities and welcomed him warmly. With Lu Lingxuan he told the emperor: "None of the sons of Emperors Xiang, Xuan, and Zhao was allowed to reign.

sentences.zh: 今至尊獨在帝位者，祖孝征之力也。

translations.literal: That Your Majesty alone sits upon the imperial throne is the power of Zu Xiaozheng.
translations.idiomatic: That Your Majesty alone holds the throne is Zu Xiaozheng's doing.

sentences.zh: 人有功，不可不報。

translations.literal: When a man has merit, it cannot go unrewarded.
translations.idiomatic: Merit must be rewarded.

sentences.zh: 孝征心行雖薄，奇略出人，緩急可使。

translations.literal: Though Xiaozheng's heart and conduct are thin, his extraordinary stratagems surpass others', and in urgent or pressing matters he may be employed.
translations.idiomatic: Zu Xiaozheng's character may be flawed, but his stratagems are unmatched and he can serve in a crisis.

sentences.zh: 且其人已盲，必無反心。

translations.literal: Moreover, the man is already blind — surely he has no heart to rebel.
translations.idiomatic: Besides, he is blind now — he cannot harbor rebellion.

sentences.zh: 請呼取，問以籌策。」

translations.literal: Please summon him and consult him on plans."
translations.idiomatic: Summon him and ask his counsel."

sentences.zh: 齊王從之，召入，為秘書監，加開府儀同三司。

translations.literal: The Qi ruler assented; Ting was summoned in, made director of the palace library, and given the additional title of grand master with the same ceremonial as the Three Excellencies.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor agreed; Zu Ting was recalled, made director of the palace library, and given the rank of grand master of the first rank.

sentences.zh: 士開譖尚書令隴東王胡長驕恣，出為齊州刺史。

translations.literal: Shikai slandered Chief of the Masters of Writing, Prince of Longdong Hu Chang, as arrogant and willful, and had him sent out as inspector of Qi Province.
translations.idiomatic: He Shikai accused chief of the masters of writing Prince Longdong Hu Chang of arrogance and had him sent to Qi Province as inspector.

sentences.zh: 長仁怨憤，謀遣刺客殺士開。

translations.literal: Changren harbored resentment and anger and plotted to send assassins to kill Shikai.
translations.idiomatic: Hu Changren, furious, plotted to send assassins against He Shikai.

sentences.zh: 事覺，士開與珽謀之，珽引漢文帝誅薄昭故事，遂遣使就州賜死。

translations.literal: When the affair was discovered, Shikai consulted with Ting; Ting cited the precedent of Emperor Wen of Han executing Bo Zhao, and an envoy was sent to the province to grant death.
translations.idiomatic: When the plot was discovered, He Shikai consulted Zu Ting, who cited Emperor Wen of Han's execution of Bo Zhao; an envoy was sent to Qi Province to order Hu Changren's death.

sentences.zh: 五月，庚戌，周主如醴泉宮。

translations.literal: In the fifth month, on gengxu, the Zhou ruler went to the Liquan Palace.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month, on gengxu, the Northern Zhou emperor went to the Liquan Palace.

sentences.zh: 丁巳，以吏部尚書徐陵為左僕射。

translations.literal: On dingsi, Minister of the Ministry of Personnel Xu Ling was made left vice director.
translations.idiomatic: On dingsi, Chen minister of personnel Xu Ling was made left vice director.

sentences.zh: 秋，七月，辛卯，皇太子納妃沈氏，吏部尚書君理之女也。

translations.literal: In autumn, the seventh month, on xinmao, the crown prince took as consort the Shen clan — the daughter of Minister of Personnel Junli.
translations.idiomatic: In autumn, the seventh month, on xinmao, the Chen crown prince married Lady Shen, daughter of minister of personnel Shen Junli.

sentences.zh: 辛亥，周主還長安。

translations.literal: On xinhai the Zhou ruler returned to Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: On xinhai the Northern Zhou emperor returned to Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 八月，庚辰，盜殺周孔城防主，以其地入齊。

translations.literal: In the eighth month, on gengchen, bandits killed the garrison commander of Zhou's Kongcheng and surrendered the territory to Qi.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month, on gengchen, raiders killed Northern Zhou's garrison commander at Kongcheng and surrendered the place to Northern Qi.

sentences.zh: 九月，辛卯，周遣齊公憲與柱國李穆將兵趣宜陽，築崇德等五城。

translations.literal: In the ninth month, on xinmao, Zhou sent Duke of Qi Xian and pillar of state Li Mu to lead troops toward Yiyang and build five cities including Chongde.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month, on xinmao, Northern Zhou sent Duke of Qi Yuwen Xian and pillar of state Li Mu toward Yiyang with an army and built five fortresses including Chongde.

sentences.zh: 歐陽紇在廣州十餘年，威惠著於百越。

translations.literal: Ouyang He had been at Guangzhou for more than ten years; his authority and kindness were renowned among the Hundred Yue.
translations.idiomatic: Ouyang He had governed Guangzhou for more than ten years, and his authority was felt throughout the Yue lands.

sentences.zh: 自華皎之叛，帝心疑之，征為左衛將軍。

translations.literal: Since Hua Jiao's rebellion, the emperor had harbored suspicion and summoned him as left guard general.
translations.idiomatic: Since Hua Jiao's rebellion the Chen emperor had grown suspicious and recalled him as left guard general.

sentences.zh: 紇恐懼，其部下多勸之反，遂舉兵攻衡州刺史錢道戢。

translations.literal: He was afraid; many of his subordinates urged him to rebel, and he thereupon raised troops and attacked Qian Daoji, inspector of Heng Province.
translations.idiomatic: Terrified, and with many of his officers urging rebellion, he raised troops and attacked Qian Daoji, inspector of Hengzhou.

sentences.zh: 帝遣中書侍郎徐儉持節諭旨。

translations.literal: The emperor sent Secretariat Attendant Xu Jian bearing credentials to convey the imperial intent.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent secretariat attendant Xu Jian with credentials to announce the imperial will.

sentences.zh: 紇初見儉，盛仗衛，言辭不恭。

translations.literal: When He first received Jian, he displayed a great armed guard and his words were disrespectful.
translations.idiomatic: When Ouyang He first received Xu Jian, he appeared with a large armed escort and spoke insolently.

sentences.zh: 儉曰：「呂嘉之事，誠當已遠，將軍獨不見周邊、陳寶應乎！

translations.literal: Jian said: "The affair of Lü Jia is indeed far in the past — has the general alone not seen Zhou Bian and Chen Baoying!
translations.idiomatic: Xu Jian said: "The fate of Lü Jia is long past — has the general forgotten Zhou Bian and Chen Baoying!

sentences.zh: 轉禍為福，未為晚也。」

translations.literal: To turn calamity into blessing is not yet too late."
translations.idiomatic: It is not too late to turn disaster into fortune."

sentences.zh: 紇默然不應，置儉於孤園寺，累旬不得還。

translations.literal: He was silent and did not reply; he detained Jian at Guguan Temple, and for many tens of days Jian could not return.
translations.idiomatic: Ouyang He said nothing and kept Xu Jian at Guguan Temple; for weeks he could not return.

sentences.zh: 紇嘗出見儉，儉謂之曰：「將軍業已舉事，儉須還報天子。

translations.literal: He once came out to see Jian; Jian said to him: "The general has already raised arms — Jian must return to report to the Son of Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: When Ouyang He came out to see him, Xu Jian said: "You have already rebelled, general — I must return and report to the Son of Heaven.

sentences.zh: 儉之性命，雖在將軍，將軍成敗，不在於儉，幸不見留。」

translations.literal: Jian's life, though it lies in the general's hands, the general's success or failure does not depend on Jian — I beg you not to detain me."
translations.idiomatic: My life is in your hands, but your success or failure does not depend on me — please do not keep me."

sentences.zh: 紇乃遣儉還。

translations.literal: He thereupon sent Jian back.
translations.idiomatic: Ouyang He then let Xu Jian go.

sentences.zh: 儉，陵之子也。

translations.literal: Jian was Ling's son.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Jian was Xu Ling's son.

sentences.zh: 冬，十月，辛未，詔車騎將軍章昭達討紇。

translations.literal: In winter, the tenth month, on xinwei, an edict ordered Chariots-and-Cavalry General Zhang Zhaoda to suppress He.
translations.idiomatic: In winter, the tenth month, on xinwei, the Chen emperor ordered chariots-and-cavalry general Zhang Zhaoda to suppress Ouyang He.

sentences.zh: 壬午，上享太廟。

translations.literal: On renwu the emperor performed sacrifices at the imperial temple.
translations.idiomatic: On renwu the Chen emperor performed sacrifices at the imperial temple.

sentences.zh: 十一月，辛亥，周鄫文公長孫儉卒。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month, on xinhai, Zeng Duke of Zhou Changsun Jian died.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month, on xinhai, Northern Zhou's Duke of Zeng, Changsun Jian, died.

sentences.zh: 辛丑，齊以斛律光為太傅，馮翊王潤為太保，琅邪王儼為大司馬。

translations.literal: On xinchou Qi made Hulu Guang grand tutor, Prince of Fengyi Run grand guardian, and Prince of Langye Yan grand marshal.
translations.idiomatic: On xinchou Northern Qi made Hulu Guang grand tutor, Prince Fengyi grand guardian, and Prince Langye grand marshal.

sentences.zh: 十二月，庚午，以蘭陵王長恭為尚書令。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, on gengwu, Prince of Lanling Changgong was made chief of the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month, on gengwu, Prince Lanling Changgong was made chief of the masters of writing.

sentences.zh: 庚辰，以中書監魏收為左僕射。

translations.literal: On gengchen Wei Shou, director of the palace secretariat, was made left vice director.
translations.idiomatic: On gengchen secretariat director Wei Shou was made left vice director.

sentences.zh: 周齊公憲等周齊宜陽，絕其糧道。

translations.literal: Duke of Qi Xian of Zhou and others besieged Yiyang and cut off its grain route.
translations.idiomatic: Northern Zhou's Duke of Qi Yuwen Xian and others besieged Yiyang and cut off its supply lines.

sentences.zh: 自華皎之亂，與周人絕，至是周遣御正大夫杜杲來聘，請復修舊好。

translations.literal: Since the turmoil of Hua Jiao, relations with the Zhou people had been broken off; now Zhou sent Chief Rectifier Du Gao on a friendly mission, requesting restoration of the old good relations.
translations.idiomatic: Since Hua Jiao's revolt Chen had broken with Northern Zhou; now Zhou sent chief rectifier Du Gao on a friendly mission to restore relations.

sentences.zh: 上許之，遣使如周。

translations.literal: The emperor assented and sent envoys to Zhou.
translations.idiomatic: The Chen emperor agreed and sent envoys to Zhou.

sentences.zh: 春，正月，乙酉朔，齊改元武平。

translations.literal: In spring, the first month, on the yiyou new moon, Qi changed the era name to Wuping.
translations.idiomatic: In spring, the first month, on the yiyou new moon, Northern Qi changed the era name to Wuping.

sentences.zh: 齊東安王婁睿卒。

translations.literal: Prince of Dong'an of Qi, Lou Rui, died.
translations.idiomatic: Lou Rui, prince of Dong'an of Northern Qi, died.

sentences.zh: 丙午，上享太廟。

translations.literal: On bingwu the emperor performed sacrifices at the imperial temple.
translations.idiomatic: On bingwu the Chen emperor performed sacrifices at the imperial temple.

sentences.zh: 戊申，齊使兼散騎常侍裴讞之來聘。

translations.literal: On wushen Qi sent Acting Regular Attendant of the Scattered Riders Pei Yanzhi on a friendly mission.
translations.idiomatic: On wushen Northern Qi sent acting regular attendant Pei Yanzhi on a friendly visit.

sentences.zh: 齊太傅斛律光，將步騎三萬救宜陽，屢破周軍，築統關、豐華二城以通宜陽糧道而還。

translations.literal: Northern Qi's Grand Tutor Hulu Guang, leading thirty thousand infantry and cavalry to relieve Yiyang, repeatedly defeated Zhou armies, built the two cities Tongguan and Fenghua to open Yiyang's grain route, and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Northern Qi's grand tutor Hulu Guang led thirty thousand foot and horse to relieve Yiyang, repeatedly defeated Northern Zhou's armies, built Tongguan and Fenghua to restore Yiyang's supply line, and returned.

sentences.zh: 周軍追之，光縱擊，又破之，獲其開府儀同三司宇文英、梁景興。

translations.literal: Zhou's army pursued him; Guang counterattacked at will and defeated them again, capturing their Grand Masters of the First Rank Yuwen Ying and Liang Jingxing.
translations.idiomatic: Northern Zhou's army pursued him; Hulu Guang turned and struck again, routing them and capturing grand masters Yuwen Ying and Liang Jingxing.

sentences.zh: 二月，己巳，齊以斛律光為右丞相、并州刺史，又以任城王為太師，賀拔錄尚書事。

translations.literal: In the second month, on jisi, Qi made Hulu Guang right chief minister and inspector of Bing Province, and also made the Prince of Rencheng grand master and Heba Lu recorder of the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month, on jisi, Northern Qi made Hulu Guang right chief minister and inspector of Bingzhou, made Prince Rencheng grand master, and had Heba Lu record the affairs of the masters of writing.

sentences.zh: 歐陽紇召陽春太守馮僕至南海，誘與同反。

translations.literal: Ouyang He summoned Feng Pu, inspector of Yangchun, to Nanhai and tempted him to rebel together.
translations.idiomatic: Ouyang He summoned Yangchun inspector Feng Pu to Nanhai and tried to draw him into rebellion.

sentences.zh: 僕遣使告其母洗夫人。

translations.literal: Pu sent a messenger to inform his mother, Lady Xi.
translations.idiomatic: Feng Pu sent word to his mother, Lady Xi.

sentences.zh: 夫人曰：「我為忠貞，今經兩世，不能惜汝負國。」

translations.literal: The lady said: "I have stood for loyalty and integrity through two reigns — I cannot spare you if you betray the state."
translations.idiomatic: Lady Xi said: "Our house has served loyally through two dynasties — I will not spare you if you betray the realm."

sentences.zh: 遂發兵拒境，帥諸酋長迎章昭達。

translations.literal: She thereupon raised troops to guard the border, led the various chieftains, and welcomed Zhang Zhaoda.
translations.idiomatic: She raised troops to hold the frontier, rallied the tribal chiefs, and welcomed Zhang Zhaoda.

sentences.zh: 昭達倍道兼行，至始興。

translations.literal: Zhaoda marched by double stages day and night and reached Shixing.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Zhaoda forced the march day and night and reached Shixing.

sentences.zh: 紇聞昭達奄至，恇擾不知所為，出頓洭口，多聚沙石，盛以竹籠，置於水柵之外，用遏舟艦。

translations.literal: When He heard that Zhaoda had arrived suddenly, he panicked and did not know what to do; he went out and encamped at Kuangkou, gathered much sand and stone, packed it in bamboo cages, placed it outside the water palisade, to block warships.
translations.idiomatic: When Ouyang He heard that Zhang Zhaoda had arrived unexpectedly, he panicked and did not know what to do. He marched out and encamped at Kuangkou, heaped sand and stone into bamboo cages, and placed them outside the river palisade to block the Chen warships.

sentences.zh: 昭達居上流，裝艦造拍，令軍人銜刀潛行水中，以斫籠，篾皆解。

translations.literal: Zhaoda held the upper stream, fitted out ships and built battering rams, ordered soldiers to hold knives in their mouths and steal through the water to chop the cages; the strips all came loose.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Zhaoda held the upstream position, fitted out his ships with battering rams, and ordered his men to swim underwater with knives in their mouths to cut the bamboo cages apart. The bindings all gave way.

sentences.zh: 因縱大艦隨流突之，紇眾大敗，生擒紇，送之。

translations.literal: He thereupon released large ships to surge with the current and charge them; He's forces were greatly defeated, He was captured alive and sent off.
translations.idiomatic: He then sent his great ships downstream in a rush and broke through. Ouyang He's army was routed, and He himself was captured alive and sent back under guard.

sentences.zh: 癸未，斬於建康市。

translations.literal: On guiwei, he was executed in the marketplace at Jiankang.
translations.idiomatic: On guiwei, he was executed in the marketplace at Jiankang.

sentences.zh: 紇之反也，士人流寓在嶺南者皆惶駭。

translations.literal: When He rebelled, scholar-officials sojourning south of the Ling Mountains were all alarmed and terrified.
translations.idiomatic: When Ouyang He rebelled, every scholar-official living in exile south of the Ling Mountains was seized with fear.

sentences.zh: 前著作佐郎蕭引獨恬然，曰：「管幼安、袁曜卿，亦但安坐耳。

translations.literal: Former adjunct of the Director of Writings Xiao Yin alone remained calm and said: "Guan You'an and Yuan Yaoqing also merely sat at ease.
translations.idiomatic: Former adjunct of the director of writings Xiao Yin alone remained calm and said, "Guan Ning and Yuan Huan, when trouble came, also simply sat and waited.

sentences.zh: 君子直己以行義，何憂懼乎！」

translations.literal: A gentleman straightens himself to act with righteousness — what is there to worry or fear!"
translations.idiomatic: A gentleman who keeps himself upright and acts with integrity has nothing to fear!"

sentences.zh: 紇平，上征為金部侍郎。

translations.literal: When He's rebellion was suppressed, the emperor summoned him as vice director of the Gold Bureau.
translations.idiomatic: When the rebellion was put down, the emperor summoned him to serve as vice director of the Gold Bureau.

sentences.zh: 引，允之弟也。

translations.literal: Yin was the younger brother of Yun.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Yin was the younger brother of Xiao Yun.

sentences.zh: 馮僕以其母功，封信都侯，遷石龍太守，遣使者持節冊命洗氏為石龍太夫人，賜繡幰油絡駟馬安車一乘，給鼓吹一部，並麾幢旌節，其鹵簿一如刺史之儀。

translations.literal: Feng Pu, for his mother's merit, was enfeoffed as Marquis of Xindu and transferred to be inspector of Shilong; an envoy was dispatched bearing credentials to invest Lady Xi as Grand Lady of Shilong, granting one carriage with embroidered curtains, oil-lacquered shafts, and a four-horse comfort conveyance, one set of drum-and-bugle music, together with banners, standards, and ceremonial staffs; his guard of honor fully matched the ceremonial of an inspector.
translations.idiomatic: For his mother's service, Feng Pu was enfeoffed as marquis of Xindu and promoted to inspector of Shilong. The court sent an envoy with imperial credentials to invest Lady Xi as grand lady of Shilong, granting her a four-horse carriage with embroidered curtains and lacquered shafts, a full drum-and-bugle escort, banners and ceremonial staffs — a guard of honor matching that of a provincial inspector.

sentences.zh: 三月，丙申，皇太后章氏殂。

translations.literal: In the third month, on bingshen, Empress Dowager Zhang died.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month, on bingshen, Empress Dowager Zhang died.

sentences.zh: 戊戌，齊安定武王賀拔仁卒。

translations.literal: On wuxu, Northern Qi's Prince Ding of Anding, Helba Ren, died.
translations.idiomatic: On wuxu, Northern Qi's Prince Ding of Anding, Helba Ren, died.

sentences.zh: 丁未，大赦。

translations.literal: On dingwei, a general amnesty was proclaimed.
translations.idiomatic: On dingwei, a general amnesty was proclaimed.

sentences.zh: 夏，四月，甲寅，周以柱國寶文盛為大宗伯。

translations.literal: In summer, the fourth month, on jiayin, Zhou appointed pillar of state Bao Wensheng as grand clan elder.
translations.idiomatic: In summer, the fourth month, on jiayin, Northern Zhou appointed pillar of state Bao Wensheng grand clan elder.

sentences.zh: 周主如醴泉宮。

translations.literal: The Zhou ruler went to the Liquan Palace.
translations.idiomatic: The Northern Zhou emperor went to the Liquan Palace.

sentences.zh: 辛酉，齊以開府儀同三司徐之才尚書左僕射。

translations.literal: On xinyou, Qi appointed Grand Master of the Palace with the same ceremonial as the Three Excellencies Xu Zhicai as left vice director of the masters of writing.
translations.idiomatic: On xinyou, Northern Qi appointed grand master of the first rank Xu Zhicai left vice director of the masters of writing.

sentences.zh: 戊寅，葬武宣皇后於萬安陵。

translations.literal: On wuyin, Empress Wuxuan was buried at Wan'an Tomb.
translations.idiomatic: On wuyin, Empress Wuxuan was buried at Wan'an Tomb.

sentences.zh: 閏月，戊申，上謁太廟。

translations.literal: In the intercalary month, on wushen, the emperor visited the imperial ancestral temple.
translations.idiomatic: In the intercalary month, on wushen, the Chen emperor visited the imperial ancestral temple.

sentences.zh: 五月，壬午，齊遣使來吊。

translations.literal: In the fifth month, on renwu, Qi sent envoys to offer condolences.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month, on renwu, Northern Qi sent envoys to offer condolences.

sentences.zh: 六月，乙酉，齊以廣寧王孝珩為司空。

translations.literal: In the sixth month, on yiyou, Qi made Prince Guangning Xiaoxheng minister of works.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month, on yiyou, Northern Qi made Prince Guangning Gao Xiaoxheng minister of works.

sentences.zh: 甲辰，齊穆夫人生子恆。

translations.literal: On jiachen, Northern Qi's Lady Mu gave birth to a son, Heng.
translations.idiomatic: On jiachen, Northern Qi's Lady Mu gave birth to a son, Heng.

sentences.zh: 齊主時未有男，為之大赦。

translations.literal: The Qi ruler had no son at the time, and for this he proclaimed a general amnesty.
translations.idiomatic: The Northern Qi emperor had no son at the time, and for this he proclaimed a general amnesty.

sentences.zh: 陸令萱欲恆為太子，恐斛律後恨怒，乃白齊主，使斛律後母養之。

translations.literal: Lu Lingxuan wanted Heng to be crown prince; fearing the empress of the Hulu clan would resent and grow angry, she reported to the Qi ruler and had the Hulu empress's mother nurture him.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Lingxuan wanted Heng made crown prince, but feared the empress of the Hulu clan would resent it, so she told the Northern Qi emperor and had the empress's mother raise the boy.

sentences.zh: 己丑，齊以開府儀同三司唐邕為尚書右僕射。

translations.literal: On jichou, Qi appointed Grand Master Tang Yong as right vice director of the masters of writing.
translations.idiomatic: On jichou, Northern Qi appointed grand master of the first rank Tang Yong right vice director of the masters of writing.

sentences.zh: 秋，七月，癸丑，齊立肅宗子彥其為城陽王，彥忠為梁郡王。

translations.literal: In autumn, the seventh month, on guichou, Qi established Prince Suzong's sons Yanqi as Prince of Chengyang and Yanzhong as Prince of Liang commandery.
translations.idiomatic: In autumn, the seventh month, on guichou, Northern Qi enfeoffed Emperor Suzong's sons Yanqi as prince of Chengyang and Yanzhong as prince of Liang commandery.

sentences.zh: 甲寅，以尚書令蘭陵王長恭為錄尚書事，中領軍和士開為尚書令，賜爵淮陽王。

translations.literal: On jiayin, director of the masters of writing Prince of Lanling Changgong was made recorder of the department of state affairs; central army commander He Shikai was made director of the masters of writing and was granted the title Prince of Huaiyang.
translations.idiomatic: On jiayin, director of the masters of writing Prince Lanling Changgong was made recorder of the department of state affairs; central army commander He Shikai was made director of the masters of writing and enfeoffed as prince of Huaiyang.

sentences.zh: 士開威權日盛，朝士不知廉恥者，或為之假子，與富商大賈同在伯仲之列。

translations.literal: He Shikai's power and authority grew daily; court officials who knew no shame sometimes became his nominal adopted sons, standing on equal footing with great merchants and traders.
translations.idiomatic: He Shikai's power grew daily. Court officials who had lost all sense of shame sometimes became his nominal adopted sons, ranking alongside the greatest merchants.

sentences.zh: 嘗有一人士參士開疾，值醫云：「王傷寒極重，他藥無效，應服黃龍湯。」

translations.literal: Once a court gentleman visited He Shikai in illness; a physician happened to say: "My lord's cold affliction is extremely severe; other medicines are ineffective; he should take Yellow Dragon Decoction."
translations.idiomatic: Once a court gentleman came to visit He Shikai in illness. A physician happened to say, "My lord's cold affliction is extremely severe; other medicines will not work. He should take Yellow Dragon Decoction."

sentences.zh: 士開有難色。

translations.literal: He Shikai looked troubled.
translations.idiomatic: He Shikai looked troubled.

sentences.zh: 人士曰：「此物甚易服，王不須疑，請為王先嘗之。」

translations.literal: The gentleman said: "This medicine is very easy to take; my lord need not doubt — allow me to taste it for you first."
translations.idiomatic: The gentleman said, "This draught is easy to swallow. My lord need not hesitate — allow me to taste it for you first."

sentences.zh: 一舉而盡。

translations.literal: In one gulp he drank it all.
translations.idiomatic: In one gulp he drank it down.

sentences.zh: 士開感其意，為之強服，遂得愈。

translations.literal: He Shikai was moved by his sincerity, forced himself to take it, and thereby recovered.
translations.idiomatic: He Shikai was moved by the man's devotion, forced himself to take the medicine, and recovered.

sentences.zh: 乙卯，周主還長安。

translations.literal: On yimao, the Zhou ruler returned to Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: On yimao, the Northern Zhou emperor returned to Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 癸酉，劉以華山王凝為太傅。

translations.literal: On guiyou, Qi appointed Prince of Huashan Ning as grand tutor.
translations.idiomatic: On guiyou, Northern Qi appointed Prince Huashan Gao Ning grand tutor.

sentences.zh: 司空章昭達攻梁，梁主與周總管陸騰拒之。

translations.literal: Minister of Works Zhang Zhaoda attacked Liang; the Liang ruler together with Zhou area commander Lu Teng resisted him.
translations.idiomatic: Minister of works Zhang Zhaoda attacked Liang. The Liang ruler and Northern Zhou area commander Lu Teng resisted him.

sentences.zh: 周人於峽口南巖築安蜀城，橫引大索於江上，編葦為橋，以度軍糧。

translations.literal: The Zhou men built Anshu fortress on the southern cliff at Xiakou, stretched great ropes across the river, wove reeds into a bridge, to transport military grain.
translations.idiomatic: The Northern Zhou forces built Anshu fortress on the southern cliff at Xiakou, stretched great ropes across the Yangzi, and wove reeds into a bridge to transport military grain.

sentences.zh: 昭達命軍士為長戟，施於樓船上，仰割其索。

translations.literal: Zhaoda ordered soldiers to make long halberds, mount them on tower ships, and cut the ropes from below upward.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Zhaoda ordered his men to make long halberds, mount them on tower ships, and cut the ropes from below.

sentences.zh: 索斷，糧絕，因縱兵攻安蜀城，下之。

translations.literal: The ropes broke, supplies were cut off; he thereupon released his troops to attack Anshu fortress and took it.
translations.idiomatic: The ropes were severed and supplies cut off. He then sent his troops against Anshu fortress and captured it.

sentences.zh: 梁主告急於周襄州總管衛公直，直遣大將軍李遷哲將兵救之。

translations.literal: The Liang ruler urgently appealed to Zhou's Xiangzhou area commander Duke Wei Zhi; Zhi dispatched great general Li Qianzhe to lead troops to rescue him.
translations.idiomatic: The Liang ruler urgently appealed to Northern Zhou's Xiangzhou area commander Duke Wei Zhi, who dispatched great general Li Qianzhe with an army to relieve him.

sentences.zh: 遷哲以其所部守江陵外城，自帥騎兵出南門，使步出北門，首尾邀擊陳兵，陳兵多死。

translations.literal: Qianzhe used his own troops to hold the outer wall of Jiangling; he personally led cavalry out the south gate and had infantry go out the north gate, attacking Chen forces front and rear; many Chen soldiers died.
translations.idiomatic: Li Qianzhe used his own troops to hold the outer wall of Jiangling. He personally led cavalry out the south gate and sent infantry out the north gate, attacking the Chen forces at both ends. Many Chen soldiers were killed.

sentences.zh: 夜，陳兵竊於城西以梯登城，登者數百人。

translations.literal: At night, Chen troops secretly climbed the wall by ladder on the west side of the city; several hundred ascended.
translations.idiomatic: At night, Chen troops stole up to the west wall on ladders, and several hundred men gained the ramparts.

sentences.zh: 遷哲與陸騰力戰拒之，乃退。

translations.literal: Qianzhe and Lu Teng fought hard to repel them, and they retreated.
translations.idiomatic: Li Qianzhe and Lu Teng fought hard to drive them back, and the Chen troops withdrew.

sentences.zh: 昭達又決龍川寧朔堤，引水灌江陵。

translations.literal: Zhaoda also breached the Longchuan Ningshu embankment and led water to flood Jiangling.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Zhaoda also breached the Longchuan Ningshu dyke and diverted water to flood Jiangling.

sentences.zh: 騰出戰於西堤，昭達兵不利，乃引還。

translations.literal: Teng went out to fight on the western dyke; Zhaoda's troops fared poorly, and he withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Teng went out to fight on the western dyke. Zhang Zhaoda's troops fared poorly, and he withdrew.

sentences.zh: 八月，辛卯，齊主如晉陽。

translations.literal: In the eighth month, on xinmao, the Qi ruler went to Jinyang.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month, on xinmao, the Northern Qi emperor went to Jinyang.

sentences.zh: 九月，乙巳，齊立皇子恆為太子。

translations.literal: In the ninth month, on yisi, Qi established the emperor's son Heng as crown prince.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month, on yisi, Northern Qi established the emperor's son Heng as crown prince.

sentences.zh: 冬，十月，辛巳朔，日有食之。

translations.literal: In winter, the tenth month, on the xinsi new moon, there was a solar eclipse.
translations.idiomatic: In winter, the tenth month, on the xinsi new moon, a solar eclipse occurred.

sentences.zh: 齊以廣寧王孝珩為司徒，上洛王思宗為司空。

translations.literal: Qi made Prince Guangning Xiaoxheng minister of education and Prince of Shangluo Sizong minister of works.
translations.idiomatic: Northern Qi made Prince Guangning Gao Xiaoxheng minister of education and Prince Shangluo Gao Sizong minister of works.

sentences.zh: 復以梁永嘉王莊為開府儀同三司、梁王，許以興復，竟不果。

translations.literal: Again they appointed Liang's Prince Yongjia Zhuang as grand master with the same ceremonial as the Three Excellencies and Prince of Liang, promising to restore him to the throne, but in the end it did not come to pass.
translations.idiomatic: Northern Qi again appointed Liang's Prince Yongjia Xiao Zhuang grand master of the first rank and prince of Liang, promising to restore his dynasty, but in the end nothing came of it.

sentences.zh: 及齊亡，莊憤邑，卒於鄴。

translations.literal: When Qi perished, Zhuang was bitter and resentful and died at Ye.
translations.idiomatic: When Northern Qi fell, Zhuang died bitter and resentful at Ye.

sentences.zh: 乙酉，上享太廟。

translations.literal: On yiyou, the emperor performed sacrifices at the imperial ancestral temple.
translations.idiomatic: On yiyou, the Chen emperor performed sacrifices at the imperial ancestral temple.

sentences.zh: 己丑，齊復威宗謚曰文宣皇帝，廟號顯祖。

translations.literal: On jichou, Qi restored Weizong's posthumous title as Emperor Wenxuan and temple name as Xianzu.
translations.idiomatic: On jichou, Northern Qi restored Weizong's posthumous title as Emperor Wenxuan and his temple name as Xianzu.

sentences.zh: 丁酉，周鄭恆公達奚武卒。

translations.literal: On dingyou, Northern Zhou's Duke of Zheng Heng, Daxi Wu, died.
translations.idiomatic: On dingyou, Northern Zhou's Duke of Zheng Heng, Daxi Wu, died.

sentences.zh: 十二月，丁亥，齊主還鄴。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, on dinghai, the Qi ruler returned to Ye.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month, on dinghai, the Northern Qi emperor returned to Ye.

sentences.zh: 周大將軍鄭恪將兵平越巂，置西寧州。

translations.literal: Northern Zhou great general Zheng Ke led troops to pacify Yuexi and established Xining Province.
translations.idiomatic: Northern Zhou great general Zheng Ke led troops to pacify Yuexi and established Xining Province.

sentences.zh: 周、齊爭宜陽，久不決。

translations.literal: Zhou and Qi contested Yiyang for a long time without resolution.
translations.idiomatic: Northern Zhou and Northern Qi contested Yiyang for a long time without resolution.

sentences.zh: 勳州刺史韋孝寬謂其下曰：「宜陽一城之地，不足損益，兩國爭之，勞師彌年。

translations.literal: Xun Province inspector Wei Xiaokuan said to his subordinates: "The territory of one city, Yiyang, is insufficient to add or subtract; the two states contest it, exhausting the army for years.
translations.idiomatic: Xun Province inspector Wei Xiaokuan said to his subordinates, "The ground of one city, Yiyang, is not worth the gain or loss. Yet the two states have fought over it for years and worn their armies down.

sentences.zh: 彼豈無智謀之士，若棄崤東，來圖汾北，我必失地。

translations.literal: Would they lack men of wisdom and stratagem? If they abandon east of the Xiao Mountains and come to scheme for north of the Fen River, we will surely lose territory.
translations.idiomatic: Surely they have men of wit among them. If they abandon the struggle east of the Xiao Mountains and turn to seize the north bank of the Fen, we will surely lose ground.

sentences.zh: 今宜速於華谷及長秋築城以杜其意。

translations.literal: Now we should quickly build fortresses at Huagu and Changqiu to block their intent.
translations.idiomatic: We should quickly build fortresses at Huagu and Changqiu to block that design.

sentences.zh: 脫其先我，圖之實難。」

translations.literal: If they get ahead of us, taking it will truly be difficult."
translations.idiomatic: If they move before we do, it will be very hard to stop them."

sentences.zh: 乃畫地形，且陳其狀。

translations.literal: He thereupon drew the terrain and set forth the situation.
translations.idiomatic: He then drew a map of the terrain and laid out the situation in full.

sentences.zh: 晉公護謂使者曰：「韋公子孫雖多，數不滿百。

translations.literal: Duke Jin Hu said to the envoy: "Although Wei has many sons and grandsons, their number does not reach one hundred.
translations.idiomatic: Duke Jin Yuwen Hu said to the envoy, "Wei may have many sons and grandsons, but they do not number even one hundred.

sentences.zh: 汾北築城，遣誰過之？」

translations.literal: Building fortresses north of the Fen River — who will be sent to cross over?"
translations.idiomatic: If we build fortresses north of the Fen, who will we send to hold them?"

sentences.zh: 事遂不行。

translations.literal: The plan was not carried out.
translations.idiomatic: The plan was not carried out.

sentences.zh: 齊斛律光果出晉州道，於汾北築華谷、龍門二城。

translations.literal: Northern Qi's Hulu Guang indeed went out by the Jinzhou route and built two fortresses, Huagu and Longmen, north of the Fen River.
translations.idiomatic: Northern Qi's Hulu Guang did exactly that, marching out by the Jinzhou route and building two fortresses, Huagu and Longmen, north of the Fen.

sentences.zh: 光至汾東，與孝寬相見，光曰：「宜陽小城，久勞爭戰。

translations.literal: Guang reached the east of the Fen and met Xiaokuan; Guang said: "The small city of Yiyang has long wearied both sides with fighting.
translations.idiomatic: Guang reached the east bank of the Fen and met Wei Xiaokuan. Guang said, "The little city of Yiyang has long exhausted both sides in fighting.

sentences.zh: 今已捨彼，欲於汾北取償，幸勿怪也。」

translations.literal: Now we have abandoned that place and wish to take compensation north of the Fen — please do not take offense."
translations.idiomatic: We have now abandoned that place and mean to take compensation north of the Fen. I hope you will not take offense."

sentences.zh: 孝寬曰：「宜陽，彼之要衝，汾北，我之所棄。

translations.literal: Xiaokuan said: "Yiyang is your vital choke point; north of the Fen is territory we have abandoned.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Xiaokuan said, "Yiyang is your vital choke point. The north bank of the Fen is ground we have abandoned.

sentences.zh: 我棄彼取，其償安在！

translations.literal: We abandon one and take another — where is the compensation!
translations.idiomatic: We give up one place and you take another — where is the compensation in that!

sentences.zh: 君輔翼幼主，位望隆重，不撫循百姓而極武窮兵，苟貪尋常之地，塗炭疲弊之民，竊為君不取也！」

translations.literal: You assist and protect a young ruler, your rank and standing are weighty; instead of comforting the common people you exhaust warfare to the limit, greedily seizing ordinary territory and bringing suffering upon the weary and exhausted populace — I privately think this is unworthy of you!"
translations.idiomatic: You assist a young ruler and hold rank of the highest weight. Instead of comforting the people you press warfare to the limit, grasping at ordinary ground and bringing ruin on exhausted folk — I cannot believe this worthy of you!"

sentences.zh: 光進圍定陽，築南汾城以逼之。

translations.literal: Guang advanced to besiege Dingyang and built Nanfen fortress to press upon it.
translations.idiomatic: Hulu Guang advanced to besiege Dingyang and built Nanfen fortress to press the city.

sentences.zh: 周人釋宜陽之圍以救汾北。

translations.literal: The Zhou men lifted the siege of Yiyang to rescue north of the Fen.
translations.idiomatic: The Northern Zhou forces lifted the siege of Yiyang to relieve the north bank of the Fen.

sentences.zh: 晉公護問計於齊公憲，憲曰：「兄宜暫出同州以為聲勢，憲請以精兵居前，隨機攻取。」

translations.literal: Duke Jin Hu asked Duke of Qi Xian for counsel; Xian said: "Elder brother should temporarily go out to Tong Province to create a show of force; I request to take elite troops in the van and seize targets as circumstances allow."
translations.idiomatic: Duke Jin Yuwen Hu asked Duke of Qi Yuwen Xian for counsel. Xian said, "Elder brother should temporarily move out to Tong Province to create a show of force. I ask to take elite troops in the van and seize whatever targets present themselves."

sentences.zh: 護從之。

translations.literal: Hu assented.
translations.idiomatic: Hu assented.

sentences.zh: 春，正月，癸丑，以尚書右僕射徐陵為左僕射。

translations.literal: In spring, the first month, on guichou, right vice director of the masters of writing Xu Ling was appointed left vice director.
translations.idiomatic: In spring, the first month, on guichou, right vice director of the masters of writing Xu Ling was appointed left vice director.

sentences.zh: 丁巳，齊使兼散騎常侍劉環俊來聘。

translations.literal: On dingsi, Qi sent Acting Regular Cavalry Attendant Liu Huanjun on a diplomatic mission.
translations.idiomatic: On dingsi, Northern Qi sent acting regular cavalry attendant Liu Huanjun on a diplomatic mission.

sentences.zh: 辛酉，上祀南郊；

translations.literal: On xinyou, the emperor sacrificed at the southern suburb;
translations.idiomatic: On xinyou, the Chen emperor sacrificed at the southern suburb;

sentences.zh: 辛未，祀北郊。

translations.literal: On xinwei, he sacrificed at the northern suburb.
translations.idiomatic: On xinwei, he sacrificed at the northern suburb.

sentences.zh: 齊斛律光築十三城於西境，馬上以鞭指畫而成，拓地五百里，而未嘗伐功。

translations.literal: Northern Qi's Hulu Guang built thirteen fortresses on the western frontier, planning them from horseback with his whip as pointer; he expanded territory five hundred li, yet never claimed credit.
translations.idiomatic: Northern Qi's Hulu Guang built thirteen fortresses on the western frontier, tracing their lines from horseback with his whip. He expanded the border five hundred li, yet never boasted of the achievement.

sentences.zh: 又與周韋孝寬戰於汾北，破之。

translations.literal: Again he fought with Northern Zhou's Wei Xiaokuan north of the Fen and defeated him.
translations.idiomatic: He again fought Northern Zhou's Wei Xiaokuan north of the Fen and defeated him.

sentences.zh: 齊公憲督諸將東拒齊師。

translations.literal: Duke of Qi Xian supervised the generals to resist the Qi army in the east.
translations.idiomatic: Duke of Qi Yuwen Xian supervised the generals in resisting the Northern Qi army in the east.

sentences.zh: 二月，辛巳，上祀明堂。

translations.literal: In the second month, on xinsi, the emperor sacrificed at the Bright Hall.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month, on xinsi, the Chen emperor sacrificed at the Bright Hall.

sentences.zh: 丁酉，耕藉田。

translations.literal: On dingyou, he plowed the sacred field.
translations.idiomatic: On dingyou, he plowed the sacred field.

sentences.zh: 壬寅，齊以蘭陵王長恭為尉，趙彥深為司空，和士開錄尚書事，徐之才為尚書令，唐邕為左僕射，吏部尚書馮子琮為右僕射，仍攝選。

translations.literal: On renyin, Qi made Prince of Lanling Changgong grand commandant, Zhao Yanshen minister of works, He Shikai recorder of the department of state affairs, Xu Zhicai director of the masters of writing, Tang Yong left vice director, minister of personnel Feng Zicong right vice director, still acting in charge of selection.
translations.idiomatic: On renyin, Northern Qi made Prince Lanling Changgong grand commandant, Zhao Yanshen minister of works, He Shikai recorder of the department of state affairs, Xu Zhicai director of the masters of writing, Tang Yong left vice director, minister of personnel Feng Zicong right vice director while continuing to oversee selection.

sentences.zh: 子琮素諂附士開，至是，自以太后親屬，且典選，頗擅引用人，不復啟稟，由是與士開有隙。

translations.literal: Zicong had long flattered and attached himself to He Shikai; at this time, considering himself kin to the empress dowager and moreover in charge of selection, he rather freely appointed people without reporting for approval, and thereby had a rift with He Shikai.
translations.idiomatic: Feng Zicong had long flattered and clung to He Shikai. Now, counting himself kin to the empress dowager and holding charge of selection, he began appointing men on his own without reporting upward, and a rift opened between him and He Shikai.

sentences.zh: 三月，丁丑，大赦。

translations.literal: In the third month, on dingchou, a general amnesty was proclaimed.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month, on dingchou, a general amnesty was proclaimed.

sentences.zh: 周齊公憲自龍門渡河，斛律光退保華谷，憲攻拔其新築五城。

translations.literal: Northern Zhou Duke of Qi Xian crossed the river from Longmen; Hulu Guang retreated to hold Huagu; Xian attacked and captured his five newly built fortresses.
translations.idiomatic: Northern Zhou's Duke of Qi Yuwen Xian crossed the Yellow River at Longmen. Hulu Guang fell back to hold Huagu, and Xian captured his five newly built fortresses.

sentences.zh: 齊太宰段韶、蘭陵王長恭將兵御周師，攻柏谷城，拔之而還。

translations.literal: Northern Qi's grand preceptor Duan Shao and Prince of Lanling Changgong led troops to resist the Zhou army, attacked Baigu fortress, captured it, and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Northern Qi's grand preceptor Duan Shao and Prince Lanling Changgong led troops against the Northern Zhou army, captured Baigu fortress, and returned.

sentences.zh: 夏，四月，戊寅朔，日有食之。

translations.literal: In summer, the fourth month, on the wuyin new moon, there was a solar eclipse.
translations.idiomatic: In summer, the fourth month, on the wuyin new moon, a solar eclipse occurred.

sentences.zh: 壬午，齊以琅邪王儼為太保。

translations.literal: On renwu, Qi made Prince of Langye Yan grand guardian.
translations.idiomatic: On renwu, Northern Qi made Prince Langye Gao Yan grand guardian.

sentences.zh: 壬辰，齊遣使來聘。

translations.literal: On renchen, Qi sent envoys on a diplomatic mission.
translations.idiomatic: On renchen, Northern Qi sent envoys on a diplomatic mission.

sentences.zh: 周陳公純等取齊宜陽等九城，齊斛律光將步騎五萬赴之。

translations.literal: Northern Zhou Duke of Chen Chun and others captured nine Qi cities including Yiyang; Northern Qi's Hulu Guang led fifty thousand infantry and cavalry to go to their aid.
translations.idiomatic: Northern Zhou's Duke of Chen Yuwen Chun and others captured nine Northern Qi cities including Yiyang. Northern Qi's Hulu Guang marched to the rescue with fifty thousand infantry and cavalry.

sentences.zh: 五月，癸亥，周使納言鄭詡來聘。

translations.literal: In the fifth month, on guihai, Zhou sent palace spokesman Zheng Xu on a diplomatic mission.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month, on guihai, Northern Zhou sent palace spokesman Zheng Xu on a diplomatic mission.

sentences.zh: 周晉公護使中外府參軍郭榮城於姚襄城南、定陽城西，齊段韶引兵襲周師，破之。

translations.literal: Northern Zhou Duke Jin Hu had palace attendant-office staff officer Guo Rong build a fortress south of Yao's Rampart and west of Dingyang; Northern Qi's Duan Shao led troops to strike the Zhou army and defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: Northern Zhou's Duke Jin Yuwen Hu had staff officer Guo Rong build a fortress south of Yao's Rampart and west of Dingyang. Northern Qi's Duan Shao led troops against the Northern Zhou army and defeated it.

sentences.zh: 六月，韶圍定陽城，周汾州刺史楊敷固守不下。

translations.literal: In the sixth month, Shao besieged Dingyang; Northern Zhou's Fenzhou inspector Yang Fu held firm and could not be taken.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month, Duan Shao besieged Dingyang. Northern Zhou's Fenzhou inspector Yang Fu held firm and could not be taken.

sentences.zh: 韶急攻之，屠其外城。

translations.literal: Shao pressed the attack urgently and slaughtered through the outer city.
translations.idiomatic: Duan Shao pressed the attack hard and slaughtered his way through the outer city.

sentences.zh: 時韶臥病，謂蘭陵王長恭曰：「此城三百重澗，皆無走路；

translations.literal: At the time Shao lay ill; he said to Prince of Lanling Changgong: "This city has three hundred layered ravines; none offer escape routes;
translations.idiomatic: At the time Duan Shao lay ill. He said to Prince Lanling Changgong, "This city is ringed by ravines on every side. There is no way out;

sentences.zh: 唯慮東直一道耳，賊必從此出，宜簡精兵專守之，此必成擒。」

translations.literal: Only the one route straight east concerns me; the enemy will surely exit by this way — you should select elite troops to hold it exclusively; then capture is assured."
translations.idiomatic: only the straight road to the east worries me. The enemy will surely break out there. Pick elite troops and hold that pass alone, and capture is certain.

sentences.zh: 長恭乃令壯士千餘人伏於東南澗口。

translations.literal: Changgong thereupon ordered more than a thousand stalwart men to lie in ambush at the southeast ravine mouth.
translations.idiomatic: Changgong then stationed more than a thousand stalwart men in ambush at the southeast ravine mouth.

sentences.zh: 城中糧盡，齊公憲總兵救之，憚韶，不敢進。

translations.literal: Provisions in the city were exhausted; Duke of Qi Xian marshaled troops to rescue them, but feared Shao and did not dare advance.
translations.idiomatic: When provisions inside the city ran out, Duke of Qi Yuwen Xian mustered an army to relieve them, but fearing Duan Shao he did not dare advance.

sentences.zh: 敷帥見兵突圍夜走，伏兵擊擒之，盡俘其眾。

translations.literal: Fu led the surviving troops in a night breakout; ambush troops struck and captured him, taking all his followers prisoner.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Fu led the troops he still had in a nighttime breakout, but the ambush force struck, seized him, and took every one of his men captive.

sentences.zh: 乙巳，齊取周汾州及姚襄城，唯郭榮所築城獨存。

translations.literal: On yisi, Qi captured Northern Zhou's Fenzhou and Yao's Rampart city; only the fortress Guo Rong had built remained.
translations.idiomatic: On yisi, Northern Qi captured Northern Zhou's Fenzhou and Yao's Rampart city; only the fortress Guo Rong had built still stood.

sentences.zh: 敷，愔之族子也。

translations.literal: Fu was a clansman of Yin.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Fu was a kinsman of Yang Yin.

sentences.zh: 敷子素，少多才藝，有大志，不拘小節。

translations.literal: Fu's son Su, in youth possessed many talents and arts, had great ambition, and did not constrain himself to minor proprieties.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Fu's son Yang Su was talented in many arts from youth, had great ambition, and did not bind himself to petty proprieties.

sentences.zh: 以其父守節陷齊，未蒙贈謚，上表申理。

translations.literal: Because his father upheld integrity and fell to Qi without receiving posthumous honors, he submitted a memorial pleading for redress.
translations.idiomatic: Because his father had died upholding his integrity after falling to Northern Qi and had received no posthumous honors, he submitted a memorial pleading his case.

sentences.zh: 周主不許，至於再三，帝大怒，命左右斬之。

translations.literal: The Zhou ruler did not assent; Su repeated his plea again and again; the emperor was greatly angered and ordered attendants to behead him.
translations.idiomatic: The Northern Zhou emperor refused; Yang Su pressed his plea again and again until the emperor flew into a rage and ordered his attendants to behead him.

sentences.zh: 素大言曰：「臣事無道天子，死其分也！」

translations.literal: Su spoke boldly: "Your subject serves an unvirtuous Son of Heaven; death is my due portion!"
translations.idiomatic: Yang Su spoke boldly: "I serve an unvirtuous Son of Heaven — death is only what I deserve!

sentences.zh: 帝壯其言，贈敷大將軍，謚曰忠壯，以素為儀同三司，漸見禮遇。

translations.literal: The emperor admired his words; posthumously enfeoffed Fu as grand general with posthumous name Loyal and Bold; appointed Su to honorary third-tier minister rank; gradually showed him courtesy and favor.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor admired his words, posthumously enfeoffed Yang Fu as grand general with the posthumous name Loyal and Bold, appointed Yang Su to honorary third-tier minister rank, and gradually showed him courtesy and favor.

sentences.zh: 帝命素為詔書，下筆立成，詞義兼美，帝曰：「勉之，勿憂不富貴。」

translations.literal: The emperor ordered Su to draft an imperial edict; he set brush to paper and finished at once, the wording and meaning both excellent; the emperor said: "Keep it up — do not worry that wealth and rank will not come."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered Yang Su to draft an imperial edict; he set brush to paper and finished at once, the wording and meaning both excellent. The emperor said, "Keep at it — do not worry that wealth and rank will not come.

sentences.zh: 素曰：「但恐富貴來逼臣，臣無心圖富貴也。」

translations.literal: Su said: "I only fear that wealth and rank may press upon your subject; I have no heart to scheme for wealth and rank."
translations.idiomatic: Yang Su said, "I only fear that wealth and rank may press upon me — I have no heart to scheme for wealth and rank."

sentences.zh: 齊斛律光與周師戰於宜陽城下，取周建安等四戍，捕虜千餘人而還。

translations.literal: Northern Qi's Hulu Guang fought Zhou troops below Yiyang city, took four Zhou garrisons including Jian'an, captured more than a thousand prisoners, and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Northern Qi's Hulu Guang fought Northern Zhou troops below Yiyang city, captured four Northern Zhou garrisons including Jian'an, took more than a thousand prisoners, and returned.

sentences.zh: 軍未至鄴，齊主敕使散兵，光以軍士多有功者，未得慰勞，乃密通表，請遣使宣旨，軍仍且進，齊朝發使遲留。

translations.literal: Before the army reached Ye, the Northern Qi emperor ordered the troops dispersed; Guang, because many soldiers had merit and had not yet received consolation and reward, secretly sent a memorial requesting an envoy be dispatched to proclaim the imperial will while the army continued to advance; the Northern Qi court dispatched the envoy with delay.
