translations.idiomatic: Before the army reached Ye, the Northern Qi emperor ordered the troops dispersed. Many of Guang's soldiers had earned merit but had not yet been rewarded, so he secretly sent a memorial asking that an envoy be sent to proclaim the imperial will while the army continued to advance. The Northern Qi court was slow in dispatching the envoy.

sentences.zh: 軍還，將至紫陌，光乃駐營待使。

translations.literal: The army returned; when about to reach Zimo, Guang halted camp and awaited the envoy.
translations.idiomatic: When the army returned and was nearing Zimo, Guang halted camp and waited for the envoy.

sentences.zh: 帝聞光軍已逼，心甚惡之，亟令舍人召光入見，然後宣勞散兵。

translations.literal: The emperor heard Guang's army had already drawn near; his heart greatly resented this; he urgently ordered a palace attendant to summon Guang for audience, and only then proclaimed consolation and dispersed the troops.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor heard that Guang's army had already drawn near, he deeply resented it. He urgently ordered a palace attendant to summon Guang for audience, and only then proclaimed rewards and dispersed the troops.

sentences.zh: 齊琅邪王儼以和士開、穆提婆等專橫奢縱，意甚不平。

translations.literal: Northern Qi's Prince of Langye Yan resented He Shikai, Mutiba, and others' monopoly, arrogance, and extravagance; his mind was greatly displeased.
translations.idiomatic: Northern Qi's Prince Langye Gao Yan resented the monopoly, arrogance, and extravagance of He Shikai, Mutiba, and their faction, and was deeply displeased.

sentences.zh: 二人相謂曰：「琅邪王眼光奕奕，數步射人，向者暫對，不覺汗出；

translations.literal: The two said to each other: "Prince Langye's eyes gleam brightly; within several paces they seem to pierce people; a moment ago when we faced him briefly, we broke out in sweat without noticing;
translations.idiomatic: The two said to each other, "Prince Langye's eyes gleam brightly — within several paces they seem to pierce a man. When we faced him just now, we broke out in sweat without even noticing.

sentences.zh: 吾輩見天子奏事尚不然。」

translations.literal: we still do not react this way when we see the Son of Heaven to present business."
translations.idiomatic: We do not even react this way when we see the Son of Heaven to present business.

sentences.zh: 由是忌之，乃出儼居北宮，五日一朝，不得無時見太后。

translations.literal: Because of this they came to resent him; they then moved Yan to live in the North Palace, audience once every five days, not permitted to see the empress dowager at undesignated times.
translations.idiomatic: Because of this they came to fear him. They moved Yan to live in the North Palace, allowed him audience once every five days, and forbade him to see the empress dowager except at appointed times.

sentences.zh: 儼之除太保也，餘官悉解，猶帶中丞及京畿。

translations.literal: When Yan was appointed grand guardian, all other offices were fully relieved, but he still retained censor and capital-region posts.
translations.idiomatic: When Yan was appointed grand guardian, all his other offices were removed, but he still retained his posts as censor and commander of the capital region.

sentences.zh: 士開等以北城有武庫，欲移儼於外，然後奪其兵權。

translations.literal: He Shikai and others, because the north city had an armory, wished to move Yan outside, then seize his military authority.
translations.idiomatic: Because the north city held an armory, He Shikai and his allies wished to move Yan outside the palace and then strip him of his military authority.

sentences.zh: 治書侍御史王子宜，與儼所親開府儀同三司高捨洛、中常侍劉辟強說儼曰：「殿下被疏，正由士開間構，何可出北宮入民間也！」

translations.literal: Supervising secretary attendant censor Wang Ziyi, together with Yan's confidants honorary third-tier minister Gao Shelou and palace attendant Liu Piqiang, urged Yan: "Your Highness has been estranged — precisely because He Shikai sowed discord; how could you leave the North Palace and enter among the common folk!"
translations.idiomatic: Supervising secretary attendant censor Wang Ziyi, together with Yan's confidants honorary third-tier minister Gao Shelou and palace attendant Liu Piqiang, urged him, "Your Highness has been estranged precisely because He Shikai sowed discord — how could you leave the North Palace and go out among the common folk!

sentences.zh: 儼謂侍中馮子琮曰：「士開罪重，兒欲殺之，何如？」

translations.literal: Yan said to attendant-in-waiting Feng Zicong: "He Shikai's crimes are grave; your son wishes to kill him — what do you think?"
translations.idiomatic: Yan said to attendant-in-waiting Feng Zicong, "He Shikai's crimes are grave. Your son wishes to kill him — what do you think?

sentences.zh: 子琮心欲廢帝而立儼，因勸成之。

translations.literal: Feng Zicong inwardly wished to depose the emperor and establish Yan; he therefore urged him to carry it out.
translations.idiomatic: Feng Zicong inwardly wished to depose the emperor and put Yan on the throne, and so urged him to carry it out.

sentences.zh: 儼令子宜表彈士開罪，請付禁推。

translations.literal: Yan had Ziyi memorialize impeaching He Shikai's crimes, requesting he be handed to the prison for investigation.
translations.idiomatic: Yan had Wang Ziyi submit a memorial impeaching He Shikai and requesting that he be handed over to the prison for investigation.

sentences.zh: 子琮雜它文書奏之，齊主不審省而可之。

translations.literal: Feng Zicong mixed it among other documents and submitted it; the Northern Qi emperor did not examine it carefully and approved it.
translations.idiomatic: Feng Zicong slipped it in among other documents and submitted it; the Northern Qi emperor did not examine it carefully and approved it.

sentences.zh: 儼誑領軍庫狄伏連曰：「奉敕，令領軍收士開。」

translations.literal: Yan deceived army commander Kudifulian: "By imperial order — the army commander is to seize He Shikai."
translations.idiomatic: Yan deceived army commander Kudifulian, saying, "By imperial order, the army commander is to seize He Shikai.

sentences.zh: 伏連以告子琮，且請覆奏，子琮曰：「琅邪受敕，何必更奏。」

translations.literal: Kudifulian told Feng Zicong and requested confirmation by memorial; Feng Zicong said: "Langye has received the order — why must you memorialize again?"
translations.idiomatic: Kudifulian told Feng Zicong and asked to confirm the order by memorial. Feng Zicong said, "Prince Langye has received the order — why must you memorialize again?

sentences.zh: 伏連信之，發京畿軍士，伏於神虎門外，並戒門者不聽士開入。

translations.literal: Kudifulian believed him; deployed capital-region troops in ambush outside the Shenhu Gate; and also warned the gatekeepers not to let He Shikai enter.
translations.idiomatic: Kudifulian believed him, deployed capital-region troops in ambush outside the Shenhu Gate, and warned the gatekeepers not to let He Shikai enter.

sentences.zh: 秋，七月，庚午旦，士開依常早參，伏連執士開手曰：「今有一大好事。」

translations.literal: In autumn, the seventh month, on gengwu at dawn, He Shikai as usual attended early court; Kudifulian seized He Shikai's hand and said: "Today there is one great good matter."
translations.idiomatic: In autumn, the seventh month, on gengwu at dawn, He Shikai attended early court as usual. Kudifulian seized his hand and said, "Today there is a great piece of good news.

sentences.zh: 王子宜授以一函，云：「有敕，令王向台。」

translations.literal: Wang Ziyi handed him a sealed document, saying: "There is an order instructing My Lord to go to the prosecution office."
translations.idiomatic: Wang Ziyi handed him a sealed document, saying, "There is an order instructing My Lord to go to the prosecution office.

sentences.zh: 因遣軍士護送。

translations.literal: He then dispatched soldiers to escort him.
translations.idiomatic: He then dispatched soldiers to escort him.

sentences.zh: 儼遣都督馮永洛就台斬之。

translations.literal: Yan sent commander Feng Yongluo to go to the prosecution office and behead him.
translations.idiomatic: Yan sent commander Feng Yongluo to the prosecution office to behead him.

sentences.zh: 儼本意唯殺士開，其黨因逼儼曰：「事既然，不可中止。」

translations.literal: Yan's original intent was only to kill He Shikai; his faction then pressed Yan: "Since the matter is already thus, it cannot be halted."
translations.idiomatic: Yan's original intent had been only to kill He Shikai, but his faction pressed him, saying, "Since the matter has come this far, it cannot be halted.

sentences.zh: 儼遂帥京畿軍士三千餘人屯千秋門。

translations.literal: Yan thereupon led more than three thousand capital-region troops to encamp at the Qianqiu Gate.
translations.idiomatic: Yan thereupon led more than three thousand capital-region troops to encamp at the Qianqiu Gate.

sentences.zh: 帝使劉桃枝將禁兵八十人召儼，桃枝遙拜。

translations.literal: The emperor sent Liu Taozhi with eighty palace guard troops to summon Yan; Taozhi bowed from afar.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent Liu Taozhi with eighty palace guard troops to summon Yan; Taozhi bowed from afar.

sentences.zh: 儼命反縛，將斬之，禁兵散走。

translations.literal: Yan ordered him bound hand and foot behind his back and was about to behead him; the palace guard troops scattered and fled.
translations.idiomatic: Yan ordered him bound with his hands tied behind his back and was about to behead him; the palace guard troops scattered and fled.

sentences.zh: 帝又使馮子琮召儼，儼辭曰：「士開昔來實合萬死，謀廢至尊，剃家家發為尼，臣為是矯詔誅之。

translations.literal: The emperor again sent Feng Zicong to summon Yan; Yan declined: "He Shikai of old truly deserved ten thousand deaths — he plotted to depose His Majesty, shave Mama's head and make her a nun; your subject for this reason forged an order to execute him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor again sent Feng Zicong to summon Yan. Yan declined, saying, "He Shikai of old truly deserved ten thousand deaths — he plotted to depose His Majesty, shave Mama's head, and make her a nun. Your subject forged an order to execute him for this reason.

sentences.zh: 尊兄若欲殺臣，不敢逃罪。

translations.literal: If my honored elder brother wishes to kill me, I dare not flee my crime.
translations.idiomatic: If my honored elder brother wishes to kill me, I dare not flee my punishment.

sentences.zh: 若敕臣，願遣姊姊來迎，臣即入見。」

translations.literal: If Your Majesty orders me, I wish you would send Elder Sister to welcome me — then your subject will enter for audience."
translations.idiomatic: If Your Majesty orders me, I ask that Elder Sister be sent to welcome me — then your subject will enter for audience."

sentences.zh: 姊姊，謂陸令萱也，儼欲誘出殺之。

translations.literal: "Elder Sister" referred to Lu Lingxuan; Yan wished to lure her out and kill her.
translations.idiomatic: Elder Sister" referred to Lu Lingxuan; Yan wished to lure her out and kill her.

sentences.zh: 令萱執刀在帝后，聞之，戰慄。

translations.literal: Lingxuan, holding a knife behind the emperor, heard this and trembled.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Lingxuan, holding a knife behind the emperor, heard this and trembled.

sentences.zh: 帝又使韓長鸞召儼，儼將入，劉辟強牽衣諫曰：「若不斬穆提婆母子，殿下無由得入。」

translations.literal: The emperor again sent Han Changluan to summon Yan; Yan was about to enter when Liu Piqiang tugged his robe and remonstrated: "Unless you behead Mutiba and his mother, Your Highness will have no means to enter."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor again sent Han Changluan to summon Yan. Yan was about to enter when Liu Piqiang tugged his robe and remonstrated, "Unless you behead Mutiba and his mother, Your Highness will have no way to enter.

sentences.zh: 廣寧王孝珩、安德王延宗自西來，曰：「何不入？」

translations.literal: Prince Guangning Xiaojheng and Prince Ande Yanzong came from the west and said: "Why not enter?"
translations.idiomatic: Prince Guangning Gao Xiaojheng and Prince Ande Gao Yanzong came from the west and said, "Why not enter?

sentences.zh: 辟強曰：「兵少。」

translations.literal: Piqiang said: "The troops are few."
translations.idiomatic: Piqiang said, "The troops are too few.

sentences.zh: 延宗顧眾而言曰：「孝昭帝殺楊遵彥，止八十人。

translations.literal: Yanzong looked at the crowd and said: "When Emperor Xiaozhao killed Yang Zunyan, it took only eighty men.
translations.idiomatic: Yanzong looked at the crowd and said, "When Emperor Xiaozhao killed Yang Zunyan, it took only eighty men.

sentences.zh: 今有數千，何謂少？」

translations.literal: Now we have several thousand — why call that few?"
translations.idiomatic: Now we have several thousand — why call that few?"

sentences.zh: 帝泣啟太后曰：「有緣，復見家家；

translations.literal: The emperor wept and addressed the empress dowager: "If fate allows, I shall see Mama again;
translations.idiomatic: Weeping, the emperor addressed the empress dowager: "If fate allows, I shall see Mama again;

sentences.zh: 無緣，永別！」

translations.literal: if fate does not allow, we part forever!"
translations.idiomatic: if fate does not allow, we part forever!

sentences.zh: 乃急召斛律光，儼亦召之。

translations.literal: He then urgently summoned Hulu Guang; Yan summoned him as well.
translations.idiomatic: He then urgently summoned Hulu Guang; Yan summoned him as well.

sentences.zh: 光聞儼殺士開，撫掌大笑曰：「龍子所為，固自不似凡人！」

translations.literal: When Guang heard Yan had killed He Shikai, he clapped his hands and laughed greatly: "A dragon's son's deed — naturally unlike an ordinary man!"
translations.idiomatic: When Guang heard that Yan had killed He Shikai, he clapped his hands and laughed loudly: "A dragon's son's deed — naturally unlike anything an ordinary man would do!

sentences.zh: 入，見帝於永巷。

translations.literal: He entered and saw the emperor in the Eternal Lane.
translations.idiomatic: He entered and saw the emperor in the Eternal Lane.

sentences.zh: 帝帥宿衛者步騎四百，授甲，將出戰，光曰：「小兒輩弄兵，與交手即亂。

translations.literal: The emperor led four hundred personal guard infantry and cavalry, gave them armor, and was about to go out to battle; Guang said: "Those youngsters are playing with arms — once you cross blades there will be chaos.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor led four hundred personal guard infantry and cavalry, armed them, and was about to go out to fight. Guang said, "Those youngsters are playing with arms — once you cross blades there will be chaos.

sentences.zh: 鄙諺云：『奴見大家心死。』

translations.literal: A rustic proverb says: 'When a slave sees the master, his heart dies.'
translations.idiomatic: A rustic proverb says, "When a slave sees the master, his heart dies.

sentences.zh: 至尊宜自至千秋門，琅邪必不敢動。」

translations.literal: Your Majesty should go in person to the Qianqiu Gate — Langye will surely not dare move."
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty should go in person to the Qianqiu Gate — Prince Langye will surely not dare move.

sentences.zh: 帝從之。

translations.literal: The emperor assented.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor assented.

sentences.zh: 光步道，使人走出，曰：「大家來。」

translations.literal: Guang walked the path and had a man come out and call: "His Majesty is coming."
translations.idiomatic: Guang walked ahead and had a man come out and call, "His Majesty is coming.

sentences.zh: 儼徒駭散。

translations.literal: Yan's followers scattered in alarm.
translations.idiomatic: Yan's followers scattered in alarm.

sentences.zh: 帝駐馬橋上遙呼之，儼猶立不進，光就謂曰：「天子弟殺一夫，何所苦！」

translations.literal: The emperor halted his horse on the bridge and called from afar; Yan still stood and did not advance; Guang went up and said to him: "The emperor's younger brother killed one man — why make such grief of it!"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor halted his horse on the bridge and called from afar, but Yan still stood and did not advance. Guang went up to him and said, "The emperor's younger brother killed one man — why make such a fuss of it!

sentences.zh: 執其手，強引以前，請於帝曰：「琅邪王年少，腸肥腦滿，輕為舉措，稍長自不復然，願寬其罪。」

translations.literal: He seized his hand and forcibly pulled him forward, pleading to the emperor: "Prince Langye is young — belly fat and brains full — his actions are rash; when he grows older he will no longer be this way; I beg you to leniently pardon his crime."
translations.idiomatic: He seized Yan's hand and forcibly pulled him forward, pleading to the emperor, "Prince Langye is young — fat of belly and full of brains — and his actions are rash. When he grows older he will no longer be this way. I beg you to leniently pardon his crime.

sentences.zh: 帝拔儼所帶刀環，亂築辮頭，良久，乃釋之。

translations.literal: The emperor pulled the ring from the dagger Yan wore, beat wildly at his braided hair, and after a long while finally released him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor pulled the ring from the dagger Yan wore, beat wildly at his braided hair, and after a long while finally released him.

sentences.zh: 收庫狄伏連、高捨洛、王子宜、劉辟強、都督翟顯貴，於後園支解，暴之都街。

translations.literal: They arrested Kudifulian, Gao Shelou, Wang Ziyi, Liu Piqiang, and commander Zhai Xiangui; in the rear garden they were dismembered and their bodies exposed in the capital streets.
translations.idiomatic: They arrested Kudifulian, Gao Shelou, Wang Ziyi, Liu Piqiang, and commander Zhai Xiangui, dismembered them in the rear garden, and exposed their bodies in the capital streets.

sentences.zh: 帝欲盡殺儼府文武職吏，光曰：「此皆勳貴子弟，誅之，恐人心不安。」

translations.literal: The emperor wished to kill all the civil and military officials of Yan's household; Guang said: "These are all sons of meritorious nobles — if executed, I fear people's hearts will not be at ease."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor wished to kill all the civil and military officials of Yan's household. Guang said, "These are all sons of meritorious nobles — if they are executed, I fear the people's hearts will not be at ease.

sentences.zh: 趙彥深亦曰：「《春秋》責帥。」

translations.literal: Zhao Yanshen also said: "The Spring and Autumn Annals holds the commander responsible."
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Yanshen also said, "The Spring and Autumn Annals holds the commander responsible.

sentences.zh: 於是罪之各有差。

translations.literal: Thereupon each was punished according to degree of guilt.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon each was punished according to the degree of his guilt.

sentences.zh: 太后責問儼，儼曰：「馮子琮教兒。」

translations.literal: The empress dowager reproached and questioned Yan; Yan said: "Feng Zicong taught your son."
translations.idiomatic: The empress dowager reproached and questioned Yan. Yan said, "Feng Zicong taught your son.

sentences.zh: 太后怒，遣使就內省以弓弦絞殺子琮，使內參以庫車載屍歸其家。

translations.literal: The empress dowager was enraged; she sent envoys to the inner office to strangle Feng Zicong with a bowstring, and had eunuchs carry the corpse home on a handcart.
translations.idiomatic: The empress dowager was enraged. She sent envoys to the inner office to strangle Feng Zicong with a bowstring and had eunuchs carry the corpse home on a handcart.

sentences.zh: 自是太后常置儼於宮中，每食必自嘗之。

translations.literal: From this time the empress dowager regularly kept Yan in the palace; at every meal she personally tasted it first.
translations.idiomatic: From this time the empress dowager regularly kept Yan in the palace and personally tasted every meal before he ate.

sentences.zh: 八月，己亥，齊主如晉陽。

translations.literal: In the eighth month, on jihai, the Northern Qi emperor went to Jinyang.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month, on jihai, the Northern Qi emperor went to Jinyang.

sentences.zh: 九月，辛亥，齊以任城王湝為太宰，馮翊王潤為太師。

translations.literal: In the ninth month, on xinhai, Northern Qi made Prince of Rencheng You grand preceptor and Prince of Fengyi Run grand tutor.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month, on xinhai, Northern Qi made Prince Rencheng Gao You grand preceptor and Prince Fengyi Gao Run grand tutor.

sentences.zh: 己未，齊平原忠武王段韶卒。

translations.literal: On jiwei, Northern Qi's Prince Zhongwu of Pingyuan Duan Shao died.
translations.idiomatic: On jiwei, Northern Qi's Prince Zhongwu of Pingyuan Duan Shao died.

sentences.zh: 韶有謀略，得將士死力，出總軍旅，入參幃幄，功高望重，而雅性溫慎，得宰相體。

translations.literal: Shao had strategy and calculation, won officers and soldiers' utmost loyalty, outwardly commanded armies, inwardly participated in the inner curtain — his merit was high and prestige weighty, yet his refined nature was warm and cautious, possessing the bearing of a chief minister.
translations.idiomatic: Duan Shao had strategy and calculation, won the utmost loyalty of officers and soldiers, commanded armies in the field and participated in the inner councils of state. His merit was high and his prestige weighty, yet his refined nature was warm and cautious, and he possessed the bearing of a chief minister.

sentences.zh: 事後母孝，閨門雍肅，齊勳貴之家，無能及者。

translations.literal: He was filial toward his stepmother; his household was harmonious and solemn — among Northern Qi's meritorious noble families, none could equal him.
translations.idiomatic: He was filial toward his stepmother, and his household was harmonious and solemn — among Northern Qi's meritorious noble families, none could equal him.

sentences.zh: 齊祖珽說陸令萱，出趙彥深為兗州刺史。

translations.literal: Northern Qi's Zu Ting persuaded Lu Lingxuan to send Zhao Yanshen out as Yanzhou inspector.
translations.idiomatic: Northern Qi's Zu Ting persuaded Lu Lingxuan to send Zhao Yanshen out as Yanzhou inspector.

sentences.zh: 齊主以珽為侍中。

translations.literal: The Northern Qi emperor made Ting attendant-in-waiting.
translations.idiomatic: The Northern Qi emperor made Zu Ting attendant-in-waiting.

sentences.zh: 陸令萱說帝曰：「人稱琅邪王聰明雄勇，當今無敵；

translations.literal: Lu Lingxuan persuaded the emperor: "People say Prince Langye is clever, heroic, and brave — today he has no match;
translations.idiomatic: Lu Lingxuan persuaded the emperor, saying, "People say Prince Langye is clever, heroic, and brave — today he has no match;

sentences.zh: 觀其相表，殆非人臣。

translations.literal: view his physiognomy — he is scarcely fit to be a subject.
translations.idiomatic: look at his physiognomy — he is scarcely fit to be a subject.

sentences.zh: 自專殺以來，常懷恐懼，宜早為之計。」

translations.literal: Since the private killing, he has constantly harbored fear; you should plan for this early."
translations.idiomatic: Since the private killing, he has constantly harbored fear. You should plan for this early.

sentences.zh: 幸臣何洪珍等亦請殺之。

translations.literal: Favored courtiers He Hongzhen and others also requested his execution.
translations.idiomatic: Favored courtiers He Hongzhen and others also requested his execution.

sentences.zh: 帝未決，以食輿密迎珽，問之，珽稱：「周公誅管叔，季友鴆慶父。」

translations.literal: The emperor had not decided; by food cart he secretly welcomed Ting and questioned him; Ting cited: "The Duke of Zhou executed Guan Shu; Jiyou poisoned Prince Qingfu."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor had not decided. By food cart he secretly summoned Zu Ting and questioned him. Ting cited, "The Duke of Zhou executed Guan Shu; Jiyou poisoned Prince Qingfu.

sentences.zh: 帝乃攜儼之晉陽，使右衛大將軍趙元侃誘儼執之，元侃曰：「臣昔事先帝，見先帝愛王。

translations.literal: The emperor then took Yan to Jinyang, and had right palace guard grand general Zhao Yuankan lure Yan and seize him; Yuankan said: "Your subject formerly served the late emperor and saw the late emperor love the prince.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor then took Yan to Jinyang and had right palace guard grand general Zhao Yuankan lure Yan and seize him. Yuankan said, "Your subject formerly served the late emperor and saw the late emperor love the prince.

sentences.zh: 今寧就死，不忍行此。」

translations.literal: Now I would rather accept death than bear to carry this out."
translations.idiomatic: Now I would rather accept death than bear to carry this out.

sentences.zh: 帝出元侃為豫州刺史。

translations.literal: The emperor sent Yuankan out as Yuzhou inspector.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent Zhao Yuankan out as Yuzhou inspector.

sentences.zh: 庚午，帝啟太后曰：「明旦欲與仁威早出獵。」

translations.literal: On gengwu, the emperor addressed the empress dowager: "Tomorrow at dawn I wish to go out early hunting with Renwei."
translations.idiomatic: On gengwu, the emperor addressed the empress dowager, saying, "Tomorrow at dawn I wish to go out early hunting with Prince Renwei.

sentences.zh: 夜四鼓，帝召儼，儼疑之。

translations.literal: At the fourth watch of the night the emperor summoned Yan; Yan was suspicious.
translations.idiomatic: At the fourth watch of the night the emperor summoned Yan; Yan was suspicious.

sentences.zh: 陸令萱曰：「兄呼，兒何為不去！」

translations.literal: Lu Lingxuan said: "When elder brother calls, why would you not go!"
translations.idiomatic: Lu Lingxuan said, "When elder brother calls, why would you not go!

sentences.zh: 儼出，至永巷，劉桃枝反接其手。

translations.literal: Yan came out; when he reached the Eternal Lane, Liu Taozhi bound his hands behind his back.
translations.idiomatic: Yan came out, and when he reached the Eternal Lane Liu Taozhi bound his hands behind his back.

sentences.zh: 儼呼曰：「乞見家家、尊兄。」

translations.literal: Yan cried out: "I beg to see Mama and my honored elder brother."
translations.idiomatic: Yan cried out, "I beg to see Mama and my honored elder brother!

sentences.zh: 桃枝以袖塞其口，反袍蒙頭負出，至大明宮，鼻血滿面，拉殺之，時年十四，裹之以席，埋於室內。

translations.literal: Taozhi stuffed his mouth with a sleeve, covered his head with a robe thrown over backward, carried him out on his back to the Daming Palace; his nose bled covering his face; he was strangled to death — at the time he was fourteen; they wrapped him in matting and buried him inside the chamber.
translations.idiomatic: Taozhi stuffed his mouth with a sleeve, covered his head with a robe thrown over backward, and carried him out on his back to the Daming Palace. His nose bled until it covered his face; he was strangled to death. He was fourteen at the time. They wrapped him in matting and buried him inside the chamber.

sentences.zh: 帝使啟太后，太后臨哭，十餘聲，即擁入殿。

translations.literal: The emperor had someone inform the empress dowager; the empress dowager came to weep — after a dozen cries she was immediately ushered into the hall.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor had someone inform the empress dowager. The empress dowager came to weep, but after a dozen cries she was immediately ushered into the hall.

sentences.zh: 遺腹四男，皆幽死。

translations.literal: Four sons borne posthumously were all secretly killed.
translations.idiomatic: Four sons borne posthumously were all secretly killed.

sentences.zh: 冬，十月，罷京畿府，入領軍。

translations.literal: In winter, the tenth month, the capital-region office was abolished and merged into the army command.
translations.idiomatic: In winter, the tenth month, the capital-region office was abolished and merged into the army command.

sentences.zh: 壬午，周冀公通卒。

translations.literal: On renwu, Northern Zhou's Duke of Ji Tong died.
translations.idiomatic: On renwu, Northern Zhou's Duke of Ji Tong died.

sentences.zh: 甲申，上享太廟。

translations.literal: On jiashen, the emperor performed sacrifices at the imperial ancestral temple.
translations.idiomatic: On jiashen, the emperor performed sacrifices at the imperial ancestral temple.

sentences.zh: 乙未，周遣右武伯谷會琨等聘於齊。

translations.literal: On yiwei, Northern Zhou sent right warrior-of-arms Gu Huikun and others on a diplomatic mission to Northern Qi.
translations.idiomatic: On yiwei, Northern Zhou sent right warrior-of-arms Gu Huikun and others on a diplomatic mission to Northern Qi.

sentences.zh: 齊胡太后出入不節，與沙門統曇獻通，諸僧至有戲呼曇獻為太上皇者。

translations.literal: Northern Qi's Empress Hu went in and out without restraint; she had relations with the monk Tongtanxian; among the monks some even jokingly called Tongtanxian "retired emperor."
translations.idiomatic: Northern Qi's Empress Hu went in and out without restraint and had relations with the monk Tongtanxian; among the monks some even jokingly called Tongtanxian "retired emperor."

sentences.zh: 齊主聞太后不謹而未之信，後朝太后，見二尼，悅而召之，乃男子也。

translations.literal: The Northern Qi emperor heard the empress dowager was indecent but did not yet believe it; later when he attended upon the empress dowager he saw two nuns, was pleased and summoned them — they were men.
translations.idiomatic: The Northern Qi emperor heard that the empress dowager was indecent but did not yet believe it. Later, when he attended upon the empress dowager, he saw two nuns, was pleased, and summoned them — they were men.

sentences.zh: 於是曇獻事亦發，皆伏誅。

translations.literal: Thereupon Tan Xian's affair also broke out; all were executed.
translations.idiomatic: Tan Xian's conspiracy then came to light as well, and all involved were put to death.

sentences.zh: 己亥，帝自晉陽奉太后還鄴，至紫陌，遇大風。

translations.literal: On jihai, the emperor from Jinyang escorted the empress dowager back to Ye; reaching Zimo, they encountered a great wind.
translations.idiomatic: On jihai the emperor escorted the empress dowager from Jinyang back to Ye; at Zimo they were struck by a violent gale.

sentences.zh: 舍人魏僧伽習風角，奏言：「即時當有暴逆事。」

translations.literal: Attendant Wei Sengjia was skilled in wind angles; he memorialized: "At this moment there will be violent treason."
translations.idiomatic: Attendant Wei Sengjia, versed in reading the winds, reported: "A violent uprising is imminent."

sentences.zh: 帝詐云「鄴中有變」，彎弓纏弰，馳入南城，遣宦者鄧長顒幽太后於北宮，仍敕內外諸親皆不得與胡太后相見。

translations.literal: The emperor falsely said "There is turmoil in Ye," strung his bow and wound the cord, galloped into the southern city, sent eunuch Deng Changying to confine the empress dowager in the Northern Palace, and furthermore ordered all kins within and without not to see Empress Dowager Hu.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor claimed there was unrest in Ye, strung his bow, galloped into the southern city, and sent the eunuch Deng Changying to confine the empress dowager in the Northern Palace; he also forbade all relatives inside and outside the court to see Empress Hu.

sentences.zh: 太后或為帝設食，帝亦不敢嘗。

translations.literal: The empress dowager sometimes prepared food for the emperor; the emperor also did not dare to taste it.
translations.idiomatic: When the empress dowager prepared food for him, the emperor dared not eat it.

sentences.zh: 庚戌，齊遣侍中赫連子悅聘於周。

translations.literal: On gengxu, Qi sent attendant-in-ordinary Helian Ziyue on a friendly mission to Zhou.
translations.idiomatic: On gengxu, Northern Qi sent Attendant-in-Ordinary Helian Ziyue on a friendly mission to Northern Zhou.

sentences.zh: 十一月，丁巳，周主如散關。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month, on dingsi, the Zhou ruler went to Sanguan.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month, on dingsi, the Zhou ruler went to Sanguan Pass.

sentences.zh: 丙寅，齊以徐州行台廣陵王孝珩錄尚書事；

translations.literal: On bingyin, Qi made Prince of Guangling, Xiaoxiao, registrar of the Ministry of State Affairs on the Xuzhou headquarters staff;
translations.idiomatic: On bingyin, Northern Qi made Prince Guangling, Gao Xiaoxiao, registrar of the Ministry of State Affairs at the Xuzhou headquarters;

sentences.zh: 庚午，又以為司徒。

translations.literal: on gengwu he was additionally made minister of state affairs.
translations.idiomatic: On gengwu he was also made minister of state affairs.

sentences.zh: 癸酉，以斛律光為左丞相。

translations.literal: on guiyou Hulu Guang was made left chief minister.
translations.idiomatic: On guiyou Hulu Guang was made left chief minister.

sentences.zh: 十二月，己丑，周主還長安。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, on jichou, the Zhou ruler returned to Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month, on jichou, the Zhou ruler returned to Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 壬辰，邵陵公章昭達卒。

translations.literal: On renchen, Zhang Zhaoda, Duke of Shaoling, died.
translations.idiomatic: On renchen, Zhang Zhaoda, Duke of Shaoling, died.

sentences.zh: 是歲，梁華皎將如周，過襄陽，說衛公直曰：「梁主既失江南諸郡，民少國貧；

translations.literal: That year, Liang's Hua Jiao was about to go to Zhou; passing Xiangyang, he persuaded Duke Wei Zhi: "The Liang ruler has already lost the Jiangnan commanderies; the people are few and the state poor;
translations.idiomatic: That year, as Hua Jiao of Liang was about to visit Zhou, he stopped at Xiangyang and urged Duke Wei Zhi: "The Liang ruler has lost the Jiangnan commanderies; his people are few and his treasury bare;

sentences.zh: 朝廷興亡繼絕，理宜資贍，望借數州以資梁國。」

translations.literal: the court raises up what has fallen and continues what was broken—by principle you ought to grant support; I hope to borrow several provinces to sustain the Liang state."
translations.idiomatic: your court restores fallen states and continues broken lines—it is only right to aid us; I ask that you lend several provinces to sustain the Liang state."

sentences.zh: 直然之，遣使言狀，周主詔以基、平、鄀三州與之。

translations.literal: Zhi assented, sent envoys to report the case; the Zhou ruler decreed to give the three provinces of Ji, Ping, and Ruo to them.
translations.idiomatic: Zhi agreed, sent envoys to report the matter, and the Zhou ruler decreed that the three provinces of Ji, Ping, and Ruo be granted to Liang.
